title: Delean-Botkin resigns from Talbot Board of Education
content: Susan Delean-Botkin stepped down from Talbot County Board of Education on August 4, 2023, due to personal reasons and her new role as Oxford Commissioner. She was sworn into the Talbot County Board of Education seat in January 2017 and served as president until December 2022. The governor's office will appoint a new board member to fill Delean-Botkin's seat until elections in November 2024.

title: Kent 4-H alumna Jill Bramble to lead National Council
content: Jill Bramble, a Kent County 4-H alumna, has been named president and CEO of the National 4-H Council. She begins her new role on August 18, following an 18-month search process. Bramble spent nearly 20 years with the organization, starting as a grant writer and rising to executive vice president and chief growth officer.

title: Community invited to celebrate completion of KI Branch Library renovation
content: The Queen Anne's County Library is hosting a Grand Opening and Dedication celebration for its renovated Kent Island Branch on August 8, 2023, at 2:30 p.m. The renovation was a joint effort between the State of Maryland, the Maryland State Library Agency, Queen Anne's County Commissioners, and community advocates. The expanded branch features innovative community meeting rooms, a welcoming lobby area, and a state-of-the-art Makerspace with 3D printers, laser engravers, and other equipment.

title: New director hired at Chesapeake College in Cambridge
content: Chesapeake College in Cambridge hired Lorelly Solano as director of the Cambridge Center on August 8, 2023. Solano previously worked at Chesapeake College as an English instructor and academic adviser before joining as director. She is a native of Costa Rica and holds degrees from the University of Costa Rica, University of Maryland, and University of Delaware.

title: Chrome City Ride raises $105K for Benedictine School
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Chrome City Ride raised $105K for Benedictine School on July 28, 2023, with over 2,100 participants from six rally points across Maryland and Delaware. The 18th annual event supports more than 200 children and adults with disabilities served by the school. Founded in 2001, the ride has grown into one of the state's largest events, raising over $2 million to date. Benedictine School serves students from MD, DE, WV, PA, and VA, and has received a two-year accreditation for its special education programs.

title: Fair offers lots of fun, much more
content: The Caroline/Dorchester County Fair took place from August 2-5 in Denton, Maryland, and offered more than just entertainment for local youth. Skylar Blunt, 17, was crowned fair queen after 10 years of involvement in 4-H, while Macrina Zbobysz, 14, won the princess pageant with her archery talent. The fair also showcased various exhibits and competitions, including a working weather goat show where Lily Hutchison took first place with her Oberhasli goat, Honey Dude.

title: For All Seasons to host Back to School Resource Fair
content: For All Seasons will host its annual School Supplies Giveaway and Resource Fair on August 16 at Idlewild Park in Easton, Maryland. The event is a partnership with Talbot County Department of Social Services, offering community resources, free snacks, and school supplies. Last year's event drew over 800 participants, and this year's event will also include vendors such as Mid Shore Behavioral Health Inc., University of Maryland Clark Comprehensive Breast Center, and Easton Elementary School.

title: School district saves thousands in energy costs - Program focuses on use and use reduction
content: Caroline County Public Schools implemented a yearlong energy conservation program with Cenergistic in July 2022, resulting in $260,000 in savings since then. The program focused on reducing energy use and use reduction through measures like solar usage and thermostats. Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons and Client Manager Scott Muir credited Josh Rein for his work in the district, which also resulted in a 35% decrease in energy use intensity (EUI) from 50 to 32 EUI. The program has also avoided 1,451 metric tons of CO2 emissions equivalent to 3.5 million miles driven by an average car. Cenergistic has a five-year contract with the school district.

title: School board adopts new AP Physics textbook
content: The Caroline County Board of Education approved the purchase of a new AP Physics textbook, "2018 Fundamentals of Physics," extended 12th edition, at its Aug. 1 meeting in Denton. The board purchased 40 textbooks for $3,375, including additional online resources, to support teachers and students enrolled in the high school advanced placement course.

title: 'Love In Action' displayed by Black Excellence fund
content: The Black Excellence Community Fund awarded $500 grants to three Lower Shore nonprofits during an August 5 evening dinner event celebrating Black Philanthropy Month in Salisbury, MD. The grantees were Y.E.E.S. W.E. C.A.N., SchooLARS 4 STEM, and Faith Over Fear Economic Empowerment Inc. BECF was created in 2022 to promote cultural awareness and pride through education, health, and welfare benefits for the Black community.

title: CATHERINE LANGSTON, GUIDING EYES FOR THE BLIND PUP GRADUATE FROM SSPP
content: Catherine Langston graduated from Saints Peter and Paul High School with Guiding Eyes for the Blind pup Grant. Catherine has raised three pups since 2015 and was awarded the President's Volunteer Service Award in 2018. She will attend Savannah College of Art and Design this fall, while Grant is going back to Guiding Eyes for the Blind training at Yorktown Heights.

title: FOR THE RECORD
content: For All Seasons will host its annual School Supplies Giveaway and Resource Fair on Wednesday, Aug. 16 from 5:30-7 p.m. at Idlewild Park in Easton. Talbot County Department of Social Services is a key partner contributing to the purchase of hundreds of backpacks pre-stuffed with supplies for community children in need.

title: Chesapeake Forum announces fall preview party
content: Chesapeake Forum announces its Fall Preview Party from 3:30 to 5:30 p.m. on August 22 at the Academy Art Museum in Easton, MD. The event is free but requires registration. Chesapeake Forum's new speaker series, Lectures on the Shore, launches on October 5 at the museum. Registration for fall classes starts on August 23, and the organization offers 36 courses this term, including a tour of the Delaware Botanical Gardens.

title: New director takes the helm at Chesapeake's Cambridge Center
content: Dr. Lorelly Solano is the new director of the Chesapeake College Cambridge Center in Cambridge, MD. She previously worked at the center as an English instructor and academic advisor before taking on her new role. Solano will lead the staff in providing services to students and community members, including workforce training, personal enrichment opportunities, and meeting spaces.

title: Doug Holly joins Chesapeake Forum Board of Directors
content: Doug Holly joins Chesapeake Forum Board of Directors, bringing over 40 years of business experience to the organization. He recently moved to Easton, MD and was encouraged by his parents to consider new ideas. Holly becomes a strong addition to the board under President Lynn Randle, starting in August 2023.

title: Mid-Shore Pro Bono interns gain valuable experience
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Three Maryland students, Clay Benedict, James Parkinson, and Gabrielle Shlikas, are interning at Mid-Shore Pro Bono this summer. Benedict is a legal intern through the University of Baltimore School of Law's EXPLOR program, while Parkinson and Shlikas are interns through MSPB's Sandy Brown Public Interest internship program. The interns have gained valuable experience working with clients on various law-related issues, including elder law, family law, and housing law. Mid-Shore Pro Bono Executive Director Meredith Lathbury Girard praised the interns' work and thanked donors to the Sandy Brown Public Interest Internship fund for supporting their stipends.

title: Backpack Giveaway - Colorful event highlights community resources
content: Over 1,500 people attended a free back-to-school backpack giveaway event at Idlewild Park in Easton, MD on August 16, 2023, hosted by For All Seasons. The event featured 25 vendors offering services and supplies, including mental health support, food insecurity groups, and translation help. Mayor Megan Cooke was present with her team from Care Packs, which feeds food-insecure students. 665 backpacks were given out to families, while the Talbot County Public Library saw an increase of 100 new free members.

title: Birds, the Brain and Plato kick off Chesapeake Forum's fall schedule
content: Chesapeake Forum launches its fall term on September 6 with a four-session course on "Plato's Republic" by Forest Hansen, Ph.D., and two sessions on birding at Poplar Island led by Kristina Motley and Wayne Bell. The organization also offers a one-session course titled "Healthy Living, Healthy Brain" starting September 7, taught by Jane Bateman.

title: Governor visits Benedictine
content: Gov. Wes Moore visited Benedictine Programs and Services on Aug. 17. He was joined by Maryland Disabilities Secretary Carol Beatty. The campus offers a year-round educational residential program for students ages 5-21 with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Maryland and adjoining states. Benedictine aims to help individuals achieve independence, but faces challenges including attracting top teachers.

title: School lunches - yesterday and today
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

1940s: School lunches consisted of biscuit with meat or cornbread, water, and seasonal fruit or leftovers; the cafeteria had a small cook, tables, and chairs.

1950s: A large room converted to a cafeteria with a big cook stove, but still shared space for gym, auditorium, and meeting rooms.

1960s-1980s: Lunches included spaghetti with meatballs, garlic bread, and salad; popular items were peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, Spam, and leftovers from supper.

1990s-2023: Schools offered a variety of lunch options, including "a la carte" foods, pizza days, taco bars, and Lunchables; most schools now offer two or three different lunch choices.

title: 4-H Development Program welcomes Japanese student
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maari Murakawa, a 15-year-old Japanese exchange student, presented to Queen Anne's County Commission on August 8 as part of the 4-H Development Program for Youth. Maari has been living with her host family, Tina Squibb and her daughters, since August. Maari's mother had participated in the program 35 years ago when she was 15, visiting Illinois at that age. The program allows students to immerse themselves in other cultures through experiential learning and cultural immersion experiences.

title: Back to school brings shopping lists, fundraisers
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 concise sentences:

Mary Hunt discusses the high cost of school supplies and technology for elementary, middle, and high school students, which totals $41.5 billion. The average costs are $1,017 for elementary schoolers, $1,277 for middle schoolers, and $1,668 for high school kids. Fundraisers, including selling overpriced items from catalogs, are a common complaint among parents, who seek advice on dealing with them. Mary Hunt invites readers to share their experiences and ideas in the comments at EverydayCheapskate.com.

title: Uncommon classes: How pop culture imagines Jesus, from cartoons to musicals - Images of Jesus have always been complex and contradictory
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Jeannie Sellick designed a course "Jesus in the Modern Imagination" to explore the relationship between religion and media, comparing ancient depictions of Jesus to modern films, comics, and music. The course examines gaps in the Bible's narrative about Jesus' childhood and adolescence, using apocryphal sources like the Infancy Gospel of Thomas. Students discuss how interpretations of religious figures are shaped by communities that imagine and re-imagine them, with a focus on the complexities of understanding Jesus. The course is relevant today as Americans debate the meaning of Jesus, with varying cultural and social influences shaping their understandings.

title: Public TV plans shows on Black colleges, universities
content: Maryland Public Television will celebrate Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) in September with its fourth annual HBCU Week. The week-long event will feature over 27 hours of content exploring the past, present, and future of HBCUs from Sept. 4-10, including special episodes and virtual events. Highlights include a "Direct Connection" special premiering on-air at 7 p.m. on Sept. 4, and two virtual events: a career opportunity forum and a screening event hosted by Morgan State University student hosts.

title: Students paying less for college than 15 years ago
content: Students are paying less for college than they did 15 years ago. Dan Currell found that colleges discovered in the late 1980s and early 1990s that high tuition was good for marketing, leading them to keep tuition costs hidden. Most elite schools could fill their annual enrollments with affluent students willing to pay higher tuition, while others use "sleight of hand" to minimize discounts. The average tuition paid by home-state public college students is about $10,000, and private colleges discount tuition by more than 50 percent on average.

title: Caroline schools serve free meals to all students - Cafeterias will still charge for extra items
content: Caroline County Public Schools are now serving free breakfasts and lunch to all students due to participation in the Community Eligibility Provision program of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Nutrition Service. The program allows free meals to students in low-income areas without application. Beth Brewster, supervisor of food services, stated that the district had already served over 3,000 students on free meals before implementing CEP. Caroline County school cafeterias will still charge for extra items like snacks.

title: FOR THE RECORD
content: Patricia Early is the director of the Talbot County Women's Club, whose president is Natalie Slater. The club had a school supplies giveaway at Easton Middle School on an unspecified date. The mistake was in a photo caption listing Early as president, not director.

title: Chesapeake Forum classes put sharp minds to work
content: Chesapeake Forum classes begin on Sept. 12 with three sessions: "Buckets of Warm Spit" discussing vice presidents during the Civil War, "The Great Gatsby," a literary analysis class, and "Sharpen Your Mind with Mahjongg," an eight-week course starting on Sept. 14.

title: It's back to school at Easton Elementary
content: Easton Elementary School in Easton, MD welcomed students on the first day of school on August 28, 2023. Talbot County Public Schools Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and Board of Education member Amy Dodson were present to welcome students. First-grader Jackson Follett attended his first day at Easton Elementary with excitement and nerves, while his mother Danielle, a new instructional assistant, also started her first day at the school.

title: Holt Scholarship Fund awards $560,000
content: The Roberta B. Holt Scholarship Fund at Mid-Shore Community Foundation awarded $560,000 in scholarships to Caroline County students. The fund was established by Haines Holt, brother of successful woman Roberta "Bobbie" Baxter Holt, who graduated from Federalsburg High School and received degrees from the University of Delaware, University of Minnesota, and Catholic University of America.

title: 'ArtScene the Podcast' features QA Teacher of the Year Andrea Schulte
content: Andrea Schulte, 2023 QACPS Teacher of the Year at Kent Island High School, was featured in "ArtScene the Podcast". Schulte studied art therapy in college and became a nationally renowned art educator, known for her student-centered approach and passion for helping students with developmental disabilities. Her National Art Honor Society students earned over $1 million in scholarship offers, while her advanced art students thrived with a 100% pass rate on AP portfolios.

title: University of Maryland Eastern Shore increases enrollment once again
content: The University of Maryland Eastern Shore increased new student enrollment for a third consecutive year, with 825 students enrolled in the fall of 2022 and an estimated 200 transfer students expected to join. Latoya Jenkins, UMES's vice president of enrollment management and student experience, said the university aims to surpass its largest class in 2015. The increased enrollment follows a national trend at Historically Black Colleges and Universities since 2020. President Heidi M. Anderson has driven initiatives to increase enrollment and enhance retention efforts.

title: Caroline schools get off to smooth start
content: Mohammed Choudhury visited Federalsburg Elementary School with retired Brig. Gen. Warner I. Sumpter on September 5. Caroline County Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons and School Principal Stephanie Brohawn greeted students at various schools, including Federalsburg Elementary and Colonel Richardson High School, which had cell phone expectations set by Principal Jared Sherman.

title: Caroline County schools welcome new teachers
content: Caroline County Public Schools welcomed 55 new teachers for the 2023-2024 school year. The orientation began on August 15 with a breakfast at Colonel Richardson High School and concluded on August 24. New teachers visited all 10 schools in Caroline County and participated in trainings, tours, presentations, and professional development sessions.

title: Constitution Day includes Douglass reenactment
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Mid-Shore Constitution Alliance will host its second annual Constitution Day celebration on September 16, featuring a reenactment of Frederick Douglass by actor Darius Wallace. The event will be held at the Talbot County Courthouse lawn and includes speakers, patriotic music, family-friendly activities, and an honor guard ceremony. The rain venue is the Talbot County Free Library. The Constitution Alliance also offers educational programming and scholarships to promote civic engagement and Constitutional IQ among students.

title: Bullying lawsuit in Dorchester County Court
content: A jury trial is underway in Dorchester County Court for a bullying lawsuit alleging negligence from Dorchester County Public Schools administrators and teachers. The case was filed by Sierra Gambrill and her parents in 2018, claiming negligence from faculty and staff at Mace's Lane Middle School during the 2016-2017 school year. Defendants include the Dorchester County Board of Education, James Bell, Cynitha Woolford, Michael Collins, and two unnamed substitute teachers. The trial is expected to conclude on Friday.

title: Dorchester Board of Education gets ready for school year
content: The Dorchester County Board of Education met on August 17 to discuss plans for the upcoming school year. Principals Gave Parker and Patricia Prosser presented their goals, which include improving student reading levels and decreasing suspensions. Board members asked about tracking progress, staffing vacancies, and community involvement. The board members discussed transparency, data-driven decisions, collaboration, and the importance of civility in making smart decisions.

title: Capital News Service compiled these stories, data
content: The "Contracted Out" project was a massive effort led by University of Maryland's Philip Merrill College of Journalism faculty and students in collaboration with the Local News Network. Four faculty members suggested the project and worked with 12 students to process data. Jerry Zremski assembled stories, while Adam Marton designed the project's digital aspects. Destiny Herbers graduated this spring with a master's in journalism from Merrill College and led the development of the web application displaying vendor payments for Maryland's 24 school districts.

title: 'Contracted Out' - An unprecedented look at Maryland public school spending
content: The University of Maryland's Philip Merrill College of Journalism published an easily searchable database, "Contracted Out," which provides a comprehensive and unprecedented itemization of school contract spending statewide in Maryland over the past four years. The database contains information from all 24 public school districts in Maryland, including vendor payments for health insurance, buses, computers, and meals, with data from 2018-2019 to 2021-2022 school years. The database was compiled by students and faculty at the UMD Philip Merrill College of Journalism over seven months, with assistance from the state's Office of Legislative Audits and other organizations. The project aims to increase transparency and accountability in school district spending.

title: Audits show trouble lurking in school contracts
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 concise sentences:

Auditors have raised serious questions about contract spending in Maryland public school districts, including Montgomery County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Charles County, and Calvert County. In May, two former transportation department officials pleaded guilty to stealing over $320,000 from Montgomery County's school system by misusing district purchasing cards. State audits have found repeated findings of problem areas in school districts, with nearly every district failing to complete proper documentation for intergovernmental purchasing agreements. Auditors have identified issues including unauthorized transactions, insufficient documentation, and excessive bus costs in multiple districts, with Calvert County Public Schools paying 22 cents per mile more than comparable districts for transportation.

title: Teach your kids about giving
content: Mary Hunt suggests teaching kids about giving by using financial principles to illustrate values such as relationships and self-worth. The antidote for greed is giving away time, talent, and treasure. Everyone possesses all three T's: time (24 hours/day), talent (special abilities), and treasure (possessions).

title: Backpack giveaway draws big crowd in Goldsboro
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

CASA of Caroline and Caroline Pride partnered to host their third annual Backpack Giveaway in Goldsboro on August 30, distributing 110 backpacks filled with school supplies to students in need. The Town of Goldsboro donated money and provided crafts and activities for kids. The event aimed to set up students for success by ensuring they had necessary supplies.

title: Create a mouth-watering holiday feast - St. Michaels classes pair students with star chefs
content: The St. Michaels Community Center is partnering with Chesapeake College to offer two holiday cooking classes: "Preparing the Perfect Holiday Meal: Turkey & the Fixins" on November 1 and "Preparing the Perfect Holiday Meal: Roasting a Leg of Lamb" on December 6, both led by Executive Chef Kerri Clear. Class sizes are limited and course fees are $95 per participant. The community center is located in St. Michaels, Maryland, and donations from its annual fund help support essential human services.

title: St. Michaels library to feature tax stamps
content: Ron Lesher, a stamp collector and judge, will speak at the St. Michaels Branch Library on October 2 about "The Taxation of Legal Alcohol During National Prohibition, 1920-1933." The event is sponsored by the Friends of the Library. Coffee and dessert will be provided.

title: Counties ponder money for college building - Financial commitment worries many of the county officials
content: Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, and Queen Anne's counties discussed a $79 million Technical Center project at Chesapeake College on September 20, 2023. The state will pay for 75% of the facility, while each county must decide whether to submit a letter of intent to provide local funds (25%). The facility, set for construction in 2026, will be over 90,000 square feet and house various trades training programs. Counties are concerned about funding due to the estimated cost, with some expressing willingness to support the project without binding fiscal commitments.

title: Commission president: 'I'm on the fence with this' - Breeding balks at Caroline's share of $94M building replacement
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

Clifford Coppersmith, President of Chesapeake College, made his case for a new technology center to the Caroline County Commission on September 5 and again at a virtual meeting with county leaders on September 18.
The commission agreed to support the project but expressed concerns about future costs associated with the 2021 Blueprint for Maryland's Future and debt.
Commission President Travis Breeding stated he was "on the fence" with the proposal, citing concerns about taking on more debt and hampering future boards' control over funding.
Talbot and Queen Anne's counties have agreed to help finance the project, but Dorchester County declined and Kent County had not made a decision as of September 18.
The commission will make a final decision on September 26.

title: Tyranny Of The Loud At Washington College
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Dr. Robert George, a conservative professor at Princeton University, was disrupted during a presentation at Washington College in Chestertown on September 21, 2023. Protesters, who were not engaged in civil dialogue, marched into the room and shouted from the start, breaking up George's talk. The event ended prematurely with George being escorted from the room, and campus security failed to intervene in a timely manner. Washington College's response to the incident is unclear, but the college's core values of integrity, civility, and free speech are at risk due to the protesters' behavior.

title: Get Outdoors Day celebrated at Hazel Discovery Center
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 sentences:

The Hazel Outdoor Discovery Center celebrated Get Outdoors Day on September 30 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., featuring over a dozen free activities led by local experts. Activities included kayaking, sporting clays, archery, fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. The event aimed to educate participants about wildlife, marine biology, and natural heritage preservation, with interactive displays and presentations by local universities and non-profit organizations. The center offered a hayride, free hot dog BBQ, and free t-shirts for kids, in a safe and supervised environment.

title: 'Fantastic job this summer' - Summer school program to expand next year
content: Caroline County Public Schools aims to expand their summer education program next year, aiming to teach 400 more students. The 2023 program, which ran from June 23 to July 27, attracted 916 students and showed success with certified teachers, instructional assistants, and site coordinators. Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons praised director Lindsey McCormick's leadership, while praising the program's goals, including boosting middle school numbers and providing career exploration opportunities for high school students. The program also saw an increase in participation from students with disabilities.

title: Raskin leads recognition of Banned Books Week
content: Rep. Jamie Raskin and Sen. Brian Schatz introduced a bill on September 27, 2023, calling for national recognition of Banned Books Week (Oct 1-7) and condemning book banning in schools and libraries. The bill has 40 co-sponsors in the House and 15 in the Senate. PEN America reported a 33% increase in book bans from 2021-2022 to 2022-2023, with Florida accounting for 40% of the bans. The Senate Judiciary Committee held a hearing on July 10, 2023, without introducing federal policies on book bans.

title: Counties ponder money for college building - Financial commitment worries many of the county officials
content: Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, and Queen Anne's counties are considering contributing $79 million for a new Technical Center at Chesapeake College. The Maryland Higher Education Commission will review letters of intent from each county by September 28. The state will cover 75% of the project's cost, with each county agreeing to provide the remaining 25%. Construction is set for 2026 and will be located next to the Eastern Shore Higher Education Center.

title: Greensboro students enjoy the great outdoors
content: Greensboro Elementary School fifth grade students went on a field trip to Tuckahoe State Park on September 25, where they navigated canoes in the great outdoors.

title: Counties sue social media over mental health in schools - Talbot among 10 counties claiming classroom distraction
content: Charles County Public Schools in Maryland joined nine other school districts in a lawsuit against Google, Meta, ByteDance and Snap Inc., alleging that social media giants are targeting and manipulating youth to stay engaged for excessive amounts of time. The lawsuit aims to pressure companies to create products geared towards children and address the negative impacts on mental health, including increased self-control issues, emotional regulation problems, and increased aggression among students.

title: Dorchester schools gain proficiency on tests
content: Dorchester County Public Schools saw increases in English language arts scores on the spring 2023 Maryland Comprehensive Assessment Program, with significant growth in proficiency from Spring 2022 data. The percentage of proficient learners for grade three to six students increased by 10.8%, with Dorchester County's average growth being 4.1 percentage points, surpassing the state average growth of 2.9 percentage points. In math, significant increases were seen in grade seven and Algebra I proficiency, while slight changes were observed for other assessments.

title: Carey Wright appointed interim state superintendent
content: The Maryland State Board of Education voted unanimously to appoint Carey Wright as interim state superintendent on October 6, 2023, effective October 23, 2023. Wright will serve until June 30, 2024. She previously served as state superintendent in Mississippi for nine years, improving the Quality Counts grade from F to C and literacy rates. Wright has a Maryland educational background, including stints in Prince George's, Howard, and Montgomery County Public Schools.

title: 'My purpose was fulfilled' - Caregiver awarded scholarship
content: Casey Hart, a Worton resident, won the $3,000 Jean Griswold Home Care National Caregiver Scholarship to pursue an RN nursing degree. Hart, who works for Griswold Home Care in suburban Philadelphia, was nominated for the scholarship due to her exceptional caregiving work in Kent County. Dr. Jean Griswold founded Griswold Home Care over 40 years ago, and the company's nonprofit organization, the Jean Griswold Foundation, offers financial support to caregivers through scholarships like Hart's.

title: 'We will celebrate some of the books that have been challenged' - Library director 'shocked' by efforts nationwide to remove controversial books
content: Arnessa Dowell became Kent County Library's Executive Director in early 2021 and has since focused on increasing library access for rural residents, including a free laptop program and expanded e-library offerings. In 2024, she plans to introduce new programming, a website, and technology upgrades. The library is participating in the American Libraries Association's Banned Books Week this fall to celebrate challenged books still available on their shelves.

title: Caroline schools, grounds spruced up over summer
content: Caroline County Public Schools Department of Operations personnel spruced up buildings and grounds over summer 2023, including installing smoke and vapor sensors in all secondary schools, refinishing high school gym floors with new mascot logos, remodeling cafeterias, and replacing roofs at Federalsburg Elementary School and North Caroline High School. Director of Operations William Mengel presented a slide show featuring the projects completed at the Board of Education's Sept. 5 meeting.

title: 'You are a 10!' - Speaker motivates, inspires at Talbot schools
content: International motivational performer Alex Boyé visited Talbot County Public Schools from October 5-9 to speak with students in fifth through 12th grade about healthy thinking and interactions. The event was part of "You Are a 10!" school tour, which aims to inspire youth self-worth. Boyé's talk was facilitated by ParentGuidance.org, funded by the MD Aware II grant, and supported by Cook Center for Human Connection.

title: Talbot Mentors celebrates recent college graduates
content: Tabius J. Wilson, Jr., Randei Collins, and Taylan Brooks graduated from college in 2022-2023 as part of the Talbot Mentors mentorship program. Wilson graduated Cum Laude from Hampton University with honors, while Collins earned a full-ride scholarship to Washington College. Brooks graduated Summa Cum Laude from Morgan State University and was selected for the President's Second Mile Award. All three are now attending George Mason University's Antonin ScaliaLaw School, Loyola University's Emerging Media program, and the University of Maryland Global Campus for graduate studies.

title: TCPS announces class of 2023 accomplishments
content:
Talbot County Public Schools announced the achievements of its Class of 2023, which includes:

* 342 graduates
* 230 planning to attend college or technical school
* 107 entering the workforce
* 5 planning to serve in the military
* 184 completing at least one Advanced Placement course
* 93 earning credit for dual enrollment courses
* 142 fulfilling Career and Technology Education Completer program requirements
* Composite SAT score of 941
* $13,865,321.20 awarded in scholarships

title: Are you smarter than a Critchlow kid?
content: Critchlow Adkins Children's Centers is hosting its annual Joy of Children Trivia Night on October 26 at the Tred Avon Yacht Club in Easton, MD. The event supports Critchlow's programming and will feature a trivia competition and fund-a-need auction. Cristy Morrell, Critchlow Executive Director, said the event brings happiness and support to working families in the Mid-Shore region.

title: VALDÉS-BRADNER WINS ANOTHER TEACHER OF THE YEAR AWARD
content: Mirta Valdés-Bradner was named 2023 Maryland Foreign Language Teacher of the Year by the Maryland Foreign Language Association at its fall conference on October 13-14 at Howard Community College in Columbia, Maryland.

title: Howie sworn into vacant Board of Education seat
content: Anna Howie was sworn in as the newest member of the Talbot County Board of Education on October 16, 2023, by Governor Wes Moore, following Susan Delean-Botkin's resignation. Howie will serve until early December 2024. She is a curriculum supervisor for Dorchester County Public Schools and has 21 years of experience in K-12 education. The Talbot County Education Association endorsed her for the appointment.

title: COLLEGE ANNOUNCEMENTS
content:
Keller Scott Daniels from Preston was named to Radford University's Fall 2022 Dean's List.
Mackenzie Werner of Ridgely received a Bachelor of Science degree in Elementary/Middle School Dual Certification from Frostburg State University in December 2023.
Kyle Hofmann, a Greensboro resident, was named to Husson University's Dean's List for the Fall 2022 semester.

title: Making history - Students work towards National History Day competition
content: Queen Anne's County history teachers Thomas Hayman and Andy Anders are recruiting students for National History Day competition. The Upper Shore region is now second in the state for participation, up from a lack of interest years ago. The 2024 NHD theme is "Turning Points in History," with projects including documentaries, exhibits, performances, and websites that can be done individually or in groups. Research assistance is being provided by public libraries across Queen Anne's, Kent, Talbot, and Cecil counties.

title: Easton grad wins DAR scholarship - Life
content: Natasha Panduwawala, an Easton High School and University of Maryland graduate from Talbot County, won the $5,000 Nannie Armistead TAnson Law Scholarship from the Gen. Perry Benson Chapter of the National Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution. The scholarship is renewable for two years and will fund her studies in international human rights law at Georgetown Law School this fall.

title: Cruise benefits St. Michaels library expansion
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

title: Washington College receives $54.7 Million from Hodson Trust - Guarantees $30k+ scholarships for students with a 3.3+ GPA
content: Washington College received a $54.7 million gift from The Hodson Trust, increasing its scholarship endowment to $170 million and overall endowment to $325 million. President Mike Sosulski announced that the gift guarantees minimum scholarships of $30,000 per year for students with at least a 3.3 GPA. The trust's support will strengthen access to education for students from all backgrounds, particularly first-generation or underserved communities.

title: Chapel District Elementary renovation design plans move to state for review
content: Talbot County Board of Education approved design development plan for Chapel District Elementary School renovation and addition, which needs to be submitted to the state for review by November 1, 2023. The project includes a full renovation and 16,600 square feet of additions, with estimated construction cost of $25.18 million and expected completion in June 2026. Design firm Hord Coplan Macht is leading the project, with Adam McDonald as project manager and architect.

title: It's in the family - Anna Howie speaks on joining Board of Education
content: Anna Howie was sworn in to the Talbot County Board of Education on October 23, 2023, after being appointed by Governor Wes Moore to replace Susan Delean-Botkin's resignation. Her grandfather and mother taught in the district, and she became involved with education through college internships. She is now the curriculum supervisor for Dorchester County Public Schools and interim principal at Mace's Lane Middle School. Howie prioritizes social and emotional learning, teacher retention, and increasing academic achievement, continuing her family's legacy in Talbot County Public Schools.

title: For All Seasons welcomes mental health interns
content: For All Seasons recently welcomed three interns: Meghan E. McPherson, Brianna Mench, and Kevin Nugent. The organization provides mental health and victim services to children, adults, and families across Maryland's Eastern Shore. McPherson is pursuing her master's degree in social work at George Mason University, while Mench is a registered nurse working towards becoming a psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioner. For All Seasons offers internships to students from various clinical settings to prepare the next generation of social workers.

title: NEWSPAPER TOUR
content: The Star Democrat newspaper hosted students from Chesapeake Christian School for a tour of their production facility. The visit was led by Jeff Wiggins, Executive Director of Production. The event occurred on October 27, 2023.

title: QA Advocates for Youth appoints new director
content: Queen Anne's County Advocates for Youth Inc. appointed Judy Corchiarino as executive director and elected three new board members: Lynn Engelmeyer, Carol Franks-Randall, and Erin Coyne. Corchiarino, a retired food service executive, will oversee day-to-day operations and serve as liaison with member agencies. The new board members are: Engelmeyer, a native Marylander; Franks-Randall, a retired educator; and Coyne, an elementary school teacher.

content: Chesapeake Forum to host final classes of fall semester on November 14 and 15, with lectures by William Messner and Jeff Macris at the US Naval Academy.

title: Denton collegian earns Meoli scholarship
content: Faith Johnson, a North Caroline High School graduate, was awarded a $10,000 Meoli scholarship to attend Penn State University in State College. The award is part of The Meoli Companies' scholarship program, which supports hardworking employees who are headed to college. Johnson worked at McDonald's in Denton, where she built relationships with people from different backgrounds and experiences. Other recipients include Jonathan Brittingham, Henry Grote, Monique Payne, and McKenzie Tubbs, who attend various universities across Delaware and Virginia.

title: Top Spellers - Ridgely Elementary's Sariah Miranda wins county spelling bee
content: Sariah Miranda won the 46th Caroline County Spelling Bee for fifth graders on October 26, 2023, at Denton Elementary School. Makayla Bowery of Ridgely Elementary took second place, while Macailey Stewart of Denton Elementary won third place. The event was sponsored by Teachers Can Help and was part of a countywide competition among elementary schools in Caroline County, Maryland.

title: Exploding pumpkins take center stage at WC - Annual event draws crowds with explosions and ooze, encouraging STEM participation
content: Washington College hosted its annual exploding pumpkins event on October 27, 2023, in conjunction with the American Chemical Society Student Affiliates Club and GAMMA ETA Chemistry Honor Society. The event drew a crowd of students, teachers, and community members to watch science-based pumpkin detonations. This year's experiments included glow-in-the-dark luminol, color changing acid and base paired with dry ice and liquid nitrogen. Sarah Arradondo, Washington College Assistant Professor of Chemistry, attended the event.

title: The Gunston School recognizes 2022-23 AP scholars
content: The Gunston School recognized 25 students as AP scholars for the 2022-23 school year, including Zachary Adams and Xuanyao Feng of Centreville. The College Board also awarded AP Scholar with Honor to Julia Buchanan and Elizabeth Parkhurst of Centreville, and AP Scholars with Distinction to Nicholas Abell and Thomas de los Reyes of Annapolis.

title: Black and Hispanic faculty underrepresented in universities
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

* Black and Hispanic faculty are underrepresented at Maryland's six largest public universities, with less than 6% of total faculty being Black and less than 5% being Hispanic as of 2021.
* Faculty demographics vary widely across universities, with some having lower representation rates than others.
* A new education code instituted in 2022 requires public universities to ensure that faculty demographics reflect the state's diverse population.
* Academia faces a multifaceted issue of underrepresentation, including hiring, onboarding, retention, and promotion, which can lead to "invisible labor" taking on unrecognized work by faculty of color.
* The gap between student representation and faculty representation has widened, with 60:1 ratios of Black students to Black faculty members at some universities.
* Tenured professors are predominantly white, with fewer faculty of color pursuing tenure.
* Initiatives such as intentional mentoring policies and best practices for increasing diversity in STEM fields aim to address these issues.

title: Talbot County resident named to Maryland Humanities board
content: Jill Ferris, an Easton resident and vice president of education and interpretation at the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum, was named to Maryland Humanities' Board of Directors on November 3, 2023. She joins nineteen other volunteers in service, bringing experience as a teacher in Queen Anne's County and recipient of awards including the Fulbright Fellowship and Maryland History Day award. Ferris will serve alongside members from various fields and institutions, supporting Maryland Humanities' initiatives to connect people, enhance lives, and enrich communities through experiences exploring shared stories.

title: STUDENT BRIEFS
content: Reilly Hawkens McIntyre of Denton was named to Iowa State University's fall semester 2022 Dean's List with a 3.50 GPA. Arianna Cintron, Alexandria Embert, Reagan Mangum, Bailey Werner, and Mackenzie Werner from the area were also named to Frostburg State University's dean's list. title: STEM festival engages youth in science, math and more
content: The sixth annual STEM Festival was held at Chesapeake College in Wye Mills, MD, from November 9-11, 2023. The event, part of the Maryland STEM Festival 2023, offered free admission and sessions on various STEM topics such as 3D printing, Python coding, and lego robotics. Navonne Owen, UME/4-H educator for Caroline County, headed the event with a crew of educators from Mid-Shore colleges and institutions, attracting approximately 250 students and adults. The festival aimed to promote STEM skills and interests through hands-on activities and competitions.

title: Art teachers recognized by Retired School Personnel Association
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 sentences:

The Talbot County Retired Personnel Association presented Fine Arts Awards to Julie Hawley and Shawn Leffler at Easton Middle School on November 9, 2023. Julie Hawley, music director, attended the University of Cincinnati's College-Conservatory of Music and Duquesne University, graduating in 2010 with a bachelor's degree in music education. Shawn Leffler, an art teacher, graduated from Buffalo State College in 2001 with degrees in art education and humanities.

title: Detecting problems with old plumbing and pipes
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

* Polybutylene piping was introduced in the late 1970s and used until the mid-1990s, but has shown to be prone to leaks and deterioration.
* Galvanized steel pipes were introduced in the 1940s and can corrode over time due to zinc coating erosion.
* Residents with homes built in the 80s or 90s may have polybutylene piping under their sink, while galvanized steel pipes can lead to water pressure loss and contamination.
* Replacing these materials is recommended to prevent structural damage and other issues.
* Homeowners can use technology such as small water alarms, whole house leak detection meters, and even water heaters with built-in leak detectors to detect leaks.

title: Elks provide Veterans Day assembly for Easton Elementary
content: Local veterans from all branches of the military visited Easton Elementary school on November 8, 2023, where they shared their experiences with fifth-grade students. The event was coordinated by Michael Feehley on behalf of the Easton Elks Veterans Affairs Office and featured speakers including Mike Detmer, a former Marine. Veteran's Day is celebrated on November 11, which marks the end of World War I in 1918.

title: Saints Peter and Paul School commemorates Veterans Day
content: Saints Peter and Paul School commemorated Veterans Day with ceremonies from Nov 6 to 10, featuring elementary students creating poppy field backdrop, middle school choir singing patriotic hymns, and high school students participating in a flag-raising ceremony and prayer service led by Pastor Father James Nash.

title: Board of Education to create Special Education Committee
content: The Talbot County Board of Education created a new Special Education Committee to modernize and fund special education in Talbot County Public Schools. The committee will be led by Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and will focus on updating practices and proposing a plan for modernizing and funding special education, with a proposed deadline of before the 2024 budget season. The committee aims to address the rapidly growing special education population and the need for a holistic approach to addressing special education in the district.

title: A year of community outreach and literacy
content: The Queen Anne's County Library is celebrating its first-anniversary of the Mobile Library initiative. The event took place on November 1 at Crumpton Park, where attendees included staff, children, families, and community partners. Tamar Sarnoff, representing the Maryland State Library, was a guest speaker. Director Janet Salazar expressed gratitude to the community for their support and highlighted the library's dedication to fostering a lifelong love of reading and learning.

title: Girl Scouts care for furry friends
content: Claire Anderson-Schultz, Amelia Beach, Clara Gerber and Ayesha Tapia, sixth graders from Troop 899 in Centreville, earned their Bronze Awards by helping the Animal Care Shelter for Kent County in Chestertown with a service project that included making handmade supplies and needed items for cats and dogs. The girls completed 20 hours of service from June to September to meet the shelter's needs, which included new cat tree, toys, pet food, treats, and cleaning items. Paige Tucker is a shelter worker at the Animal Care Shelter in Chestertown. Allison Otadan shared the shelter is grateful for the efforts of the girls.

title: High school students become college scientists
content: Students from Queen Anne's County High School worked alongside college chemistry students at Washington College on November 14-15, 2023. The partnership was developed by Michael Geoffroy and Leslie Sherman to provide high schoolers with college-level experience. Students worked in modern lab facilities under the supervision of professors like Betsy Moyer-Taylor, Jeremy Bard, and Frank Keegan.

title: Education foundation established in Caroline - Four local leaders spearhead funding financial literacy opportunities for students
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 concise sentences:

Four local leaders - Tolbert Rowe, Robert Willey, Dr. James Orr Jr., and Wayne Cole - established the Caroline County Education Foundation on Oct. 5 with funding financial literacy opportunities for students. The foundation was previously launched in 1987 but ceased operations due to lack of recruitment and energy. The new foundation aims to preserve the intent of the previous donors' seed money, focusing initially on financial literacy, career exploration, and entrepreneurship education. Caroline County Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons supports the foundation's efforts, citing the need for financial literacy in light of the Blueprint for Maryland Education's unfunded mandate.

title: College Board honors Caroline students
content: Twelve Caroline County Public Schools students earned academic honors from the College Board's National Recognition Programs, recognized at the November 7 Board of Education meeting. The recipients include Emmy Brown-Varon, Rebeccah Chambers, Leland Courie, Felix Fimbres, Brooke Gauck, Dallas Helsel, Shelby MacFarland, Leslie Monter Casio, Molly Coughenour, Riley Schall, Eric Shockley, and Bailey Thayer.

title: CCTC AMP students present designs - Rashad Wilson's winning design adorns dartboard cabinet project
content: The seventh cohort of Advanced Manufacturing Program students at Caroline Career and Technology Center presented design ideas for their dartboard cabinet project on October 26, 2023. Rashad Wilson's winning design was inspired by saloon doors in the Old West. The program began three years ago when a student approached Keith Hale with the idea to manufacture dartboard cabinets. The class has since become popular, selling out before being presented.

title: PES teacher wins McNeely Award
content: Christi Saylor, a physical education teacher at Preston Elementary School in Denton, received the Simon A. McNeely Award from SHAPE Maryland on November 7, 2023. She was recognized for her outstanding teaching and service innovations as well as being actively involved in school and community affairs. Saylor must have been a member of SHAPE Maryland or a related organization with at least five years of professional experience to be eligible for the award.

title: Opening Doors (Again) For Literacy
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Ashley Singer and Julie Blyman, founders of Open Doors Partners in Education, faced a $40,000 loss after their office caught fire in September. The organization, founded in 2020 as a response to COVID-19 pandemic learning losses, has assisted over 100 students in Kent County with literacy training using the Orton-Gillingham method. The group received significant community support and now resides at 116-D South Lynchburg Street in Chestertown, Maryland, with plans for a ribbon-cutting ceremony on December 1.

title: Apprenticeships explored at local high schools
content: Queen Anne's County in Maryland is revitalizing career apprenticeships for high school students through a new program, with Career Coaches Karen Hesson and Betsy Ricketts assisting students. The county created this position to help students navigate career options, including college, trade schools, and working directly with businesses. Connie Dean, from the Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development department, is helping secure partnering businesses for apprenticeships, which involve 450 hours of work to earn recognition. Three Kent Island students completed culinary training at Chesapeake College this semester, while others participated in a military and law enforcement day during the apprentice week.

title: Centreville Rotary receives Rotary International Award
content: Centreville Rotary Club received the Rotary Citation Award for its support in community service and leadership development during the 2022-2023 Rotary Year. The club was one of ten clubs in Rotary District 7630 to receive the award, recognized by Immediate Past International President Jennifer Jones. Centreville Rotary Club, established in 1927, also received the "100% Foundation Giving Banner" and the "Every Rotarian, Every Year Banner" for its contributions to the Rotary Foundation.

title: MCAP results show signs of recovery from pandemic learning loss - Science scores still show decline
content: Maryland Comprehensive Assessment Program (MCAP) test results show that student proficiency in English Language Arts has surpassed pre-pandemic levels, with an average passing rate of 47% in 2023. Math scores have improved but still lag behind pre-pandemic levels, with a 24% average passing rate in 2023. Science scores, particularly for grade 8, continue to decline, with a historic low in 2023.

title: Scholar to discuss Anna Douglass
content: Dr. Celeste-Marie Bernier will discuss Anna Murray Douglass at the Museum of Rural Life in Denton, MD on November 29, from 5 to 6:30 p.m. The event is co-sponsored by the Caroline County Public Library and the Frederick Douglass Honor Society.

title: 'I hope we inspire kids to cook' - Easton High School Culinary Program cranks out hundreds of holiday pies
content: Easton High School Culinary Program produced hundreds of holiday pies, cakes, and cookies with ingredients from local farmers, including Caroline County-grown sweet potatoes. The program, led by instructor Linda Brown for 48 years, has a flexible student population that often goes on to culinary schools like CIA or Johnson and Wales. Students, including Francis Blazejak and Harlin Bartolon, donated their time and skills to the effort, which aims to inspire kids to cook and raise funds through bake sales.

title: Caroline Commissioners approve summer school grant
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

The Caroline County Commission approved a three-year $1.2 million grant from the Maryland Department of Education to fund summer learning centers for 1,100 students in 2024 and 400 students in 2025-2026. The commission also approved a contract with Wellpath LLC for medical services at the county jail and offered surplus vehicles for auction. Commission President Travis Breeding discussed reconfiguring the director of Public Works position, citing concerns about its scope and potential need to be contracted out.

title: School principals prepare for the Blueprint For Maryland's Future
content: Maryland's School Leaders Conference discussed the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, a 2021 education reform law that aims to address challenges in the state's education system. The plan was established by the Kirwan Commission in 2016 and allocates $3.8 billion over 10 years. The state will fund socioeconomically integrated pre-K programs through public schools and private providers. The Blueprint also seeks to make students college and career ready by 10th grade, with curriculum changes, apprenticeships, and technical education programs.

title: Caroline County Public Schools Concert Schedule
content: Caroline County Public Schools will host various winter concerts at schools between December 13 and December 22, 2023, including Federalsburg ES, Greensboro ES, Lockerman MS, Denton ES, Preston ES, Ridgely ES, North Caroline HS, and Colonel Richardson HS.

title: Ccps Sophomores Explore Career Options At Rotary Fair
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 4 sentences:

The Denton Rotary's 10th Grade Career Exploration Fair was held on November 21, 2023, at the General James F. Fretterd Community Center. The event was attended by 97 students from Colonial Richardson High School, North County High School, and the Caroline Career and Technology Center. Representatives from over 30 businesses and organizations participated in the fair, offering vendor exhibits, workshops, and career guidance to students. The event was sponsored by several local businesses and schools, including Smiles by Holsinger, Shore United Bank, Summit Community Bank, and Chesapeake College.

title: DECEMBER at Chesapeake College
content: Chesapeake College will host "THE SNOW SHOW" holiday musical production at TPAC on December 8-9 and 12-14. Info sessions for truck driving careers, skilled trades programs, and winter break schedules are scheduled. The college is closed from December 20-24 and classes begin January 8-9 for entry-level marine service technician and V6 engine service students.

title: Superintendent Outlines Budget Priorities, Timeline
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Dr. Derek Simmons, Superintendent of Caroline County Public Schools, outlined budget priorities and timeline for fiscal year 2025 due to uncertain Blueprint demands and decreasing pandemic-related grant funding. The Board of Education approved a revised timeline to move Simmons's final budget proposal from February to April. Key challenges include meeting dual enrollment requirements and starting teacher salaries, as well as decreasing state and federal funding.

title: Class Of 1983 Celebrates 40Th Reunion
content: The Easton High School Class of 1983 celebrated its 40th reunion on September 23 at American Legion Post #91 in Cambridge, Maryland. Thirty-four classmates attended, including two from Florida and Georgia. The event honored the memory of several classmates and featured a dinner, dancing, and storytelling.

title: Lockerman Middle Receives Stem Donation
content: Lockerman Middle School received a donation of $40,000 worth of STEM kits from the Cal Ripken, Sr. Foundation, made possible by a grant from the University of Maryland Medical System Foundation. The donation includes curriculum guidance and an online portal with cross-curricular lesson plans and resources. Teachers were introduced to the materials during a professional development day in November.

title: Caroline Students Earn Biliteracy Credentials
content: Caroline County students earned the Global Seal of Biliteracy, a language credential issued by an independent international certifying body, on December 5, 2023. The students achieved high proficiency in two or more languages to earn advanced placement, scholarships, and employment opportunities. The recipients include 17 Caroline County students, with North Caroline High School Spanish language teacher Mirta Valdes-Bradner receiving the 2023 Minority Recognition Award from the Maryland State Educators Association in June 2023.

title: Tcps Gives Update On Its Priorities At Board Meeting
content: Talbot County Public Schools' Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi reported on the school system's priorities, which include academic equity and achievement, fostering an engaging environment, and hiring and retaining highly qualified and diverse staff. Academic equity and achievement strategies included implementing additional interventions and assessments, while fostering an engaging environment involved school-based mental health services and restorative practices training. The district has seen improvement in student and teacher attitudes towards safety and substance abuse since conducting climate surveys in 2022. Since the start of the year, TCPS has hired 90 new staff members, with a focus on retaining existing employees to address national education shortages.

title: Local Student Selected For General Assembly Page Program
content: William O'Donnell, an Easton High School senior, has been chosen to represent Talbot County in the Maryland General Assembly Student Page Program for the 2024 Legislative Session. He previously served on the Maryland Youth Advisory Council and holds various leadership positions. The program was established in 1970 and selects 105 student pages annually from across Maryland.

title: Student designs school district holiday card
content: Summer Smith's artwork was chosen for the annual Caroline County Public Schools holiday card. The artwork was unveiled at a Dec. 5 board of education meeting and resulted in Summer being presented with a certificate by Superintendent Derek Simmons. Smith's design featured intricate details such as footsteps leading from a snowman to a cabin, smoke rising from the chimney, and script in the trees.

title: Talbot senior center opens upgraded computer lab
content: Talbot County Senior Center at Brookletts in Easton, Maryland opened an upgraded computer lab funded by a $33,356 T-Mobile Hometown Grant. The lab features 20 new computer stations and was made possible through a grant to Upper Shore Aging, Inc., a nonprofit organization serving Talbot, Caroline, and Kent counties.

title: Holiday de-stress - Celebration alleviates overstimulation associated with holidays
content: The Sensory Holiday Celebration was held at Kent County Middle School on December 27 in its sixth year, organized by the Kent County Infants and Toddlers program. The event catered to children with disabilities such as autism due to overstimulation concerns. It featured Santa Claus, crafts, and gifts, including a "Nice List Certification" from Santa's desk. Professionals from various organizations attended, including staff from Judy Centers in Kent County and the Family Resource Center.

title: Cambridge Rotary Club rings in holiday season at Walmart
content: The Rotary Club of Cambridge rang the bell at Walmart on December 29, 2023, as part of their annual holiday tradition with the Salvation Army. The event was joined by members of the Cambridge South Dorchester High School Interact Club, including President Mia Jackson and Vice President Tyler Sears. In recent years, the high school club has been helping the Rotary Club in giving back to the community.

title: Character Counts - Queen Anne's County commissioners recognize Gavin Schulte
content: Queen Anne's County commissioners recognized Gavin Schulte for his Character Counts Spotlight on Caring. Schulte is a Kent Island High School junior who started showing caring at Matapeake Elementary School and began organizing coat drives and food collections in 2019. He reached out to Jone Taylor of Queen Anne's County Social Services, packing duffel bags with essential items for foster children. Gavin Schulte was presented with the Character Counts Spotlight award by Commissioner Philip L. Dumenil on January 3, 2024.

title: School board posts highlights, next meetings
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 3-5 concise sentences:

Caroline County Board of Education met on Dec. 5 and reelected board President Rick Barton and Vice President Jones. Erin Thornton provided a finance report for the period ending Nov. 30, 2023, citing 74% budget expenditure, with overages in Special Education, Transportation salaries, and Capital outlay. The next Board meetings are scheduled for Jan. 9 and Jan. 16.

title: Talbot County Garden Club announces winter lecture series
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Talbot County Garden Club announced its 2024 winter lecture series featuring expert insights and tips on florals and gardens. Presenters include Leslie Harris (Jan. 23) and Eva Monheim (Feb. 27). The lectures, held at the Talbot County Free Library in Easton, are free and open to the public. A sneak peek preview is scheduled for March 27, led by event co-chairs Zandi Nammack and Kim Eckert.

title: Student published before graduation
content: Natalie Martinaitis published her first book "The Post-PSO Project" on December 11, 2023, at Washington College in Maryland. The novella takes place in a world where psychological experiments are carried out on children on Earth and Mars by the People Stimulus Organization (PSO). Martinaitis plans to submit her next two books, "Elliot's Story" and "Demons", for publication and aims to win the Sophie Kerr Prize after graduation.

title: Problems persist in juvenile services schooling
content: The article discusses problems persisting in juvenile services schooling in Maryland, specifically at the Victor Cullen Center. The school faces challenges such as teacher vacancies of 30%, streaming instruction, and low pay, which have led to tensions between education and Juvenile Services agencies. Two years after the General Assembly transferred responsibility for incarcerated students' education, students continue to face issues like inadequate services for learning disabled students and high staff turnover.

title: Radcliffe Creek School awarded 'social-emotional' learning grant
content: Radcliffe Creek School was awarded a grant from the Queen Anne's County Mental Health Committee to expand its social-emotional learning curriculum. The grant will bring additional curriculums, Brain Talk and Conscious Discipline, to older students and their families. Radcliffe Creek School Head of School Peter Thayer said the funding will help meet the needs of neurodivergent students. The QACMHC President Kelly Phipps credited community support for the grant, which will also bring social-emotional programming to the local community starting in 2024.

title: 'Diving Deep' with dyslexia: Local special education teacher works to raise awareness
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Robin Williams, Jay Leno, and other famous figures had dyslexia. Lindsey Parte, a Special Education teacher in Stevensville, Maryland, reignited the Decoding Dyslexia Maryland Eastern Shore Chapter to raise awareness about dyslexia, especially for children. Parte's son Lincoln was diagnosed with dyslexia at age 8, but she suspected it earlier due to his struggles with reading. The Mayo Clinic states that dyslexia is a learning disorder involving difficulty decoding speech sounds and letters.

title: DCTC Masonry instructor surprised by coworkers on last day
content: Masonry Instructor Eddie Bailey was surprised by coworkers at his last day of teaching on January 5, 2024, at Dorchester Career and Technology Center in Cambridge, MD. His coworkers wore similar outfits to his, including grey sweatshirts and jeans, with fake metal detectors. DCTC Principal Ashley Robinson organized the surprise as part of the school's holiday spirit week. Bailey plans to retire from teaching and continue exploring his hobby of metal detecting, a passion he developed over the past five years.

title: Some thoughts on those New Year's resolutions
content: David Reel's top New Year's resolution for 2024 is to use new approaches to convert more resolutions into accomplishments. He emphasizes embracing a sense of urgency, as described by Professor John Kotter, and setting SMART (Specific, Measurable, Audacious, Realistic, Time-sensitive) goals, with tactics developed in priority order to achieve them.

title: Superintendent of schools to retire in 2024
content: Kent County Public Schools' Superintendent Dr. Karen Couch will retire June 30, 2024. She was named Maryland Superintendent of the Year in 2021 and previously served as superintendent of the Moriarty-Edgewood School District from 2001 to 2013. The Board of Education is holding a special meeting on January 23 to discuss the search for her successor, led by President Joe Goetz and Vice President Francoise Sullivan.

title: Alpha Delta Kappa celebrates the holidays, welcomes new members
content: Xi Chapter of Alpha Delta Kappa held its annual Christmas Fraternity Education meeting on January 11, 2024, at the Tidewater Inn in Easton, MD, with President Pat Clark welcoming new members Peggy Harrington and Cathy Grantham, among others. The initiation ceremony included Debbie Garner, an Easton resident, who was sponsored by Pat Clark. The chapter also participated in a book exchange and had a holiday gathering.

title: CBMM’s Shipyard offers 'Apprentice for a Day' programs
content:
CBMM's Shipyard offers "Apprentice for a Day" programs with hands-on experiences on winter Saturdays. Programs include:
- Shipyard Workdays on Feb 3, Feb 17, March 9, and March 30
- Leather Working Workshop (Jan 27-28)
- Dovetail "Ditty Box" Workshop (Feb 23-25)
- Marine welding course in partnership with Chesapeake College (March 22-24)

title: Wye River Upper School continuing eighth-grade program
content: Wye River Upper School has continued its eighth-grade program, a pilot initiative launched in September to enhance high school readiness and reduce transition anxiety. The first class of students successfully completed the program. Prospective students and parents are invited to an open house event on January 25 at 10:30 a.m. Wye River Upper School is located in Centreville.

title: Denton Elementary principal earns doctorate
content: Denton Elementary principal Dr. Sarah Crebs-Oberdorf earned her doctoral degree in contemporary literacy studies from Salisbury University on Nov. 27, 2023. She defended her dissertation titled "An Inquiry Into a Collaborative Teacher Study Group: How do Elementary Teachers of Reading talk about the Intersection Between Race and Reading Instruction and Assessment?" on Jan. 9, 2024, with CCPS Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons in attendance. Crebs-Oberdorf began her career as a special education teacher in Caroline County districts and served as assistant principal at Ridgely Elementary School.

title: Blueprint pillar chairs share Caroline's progress
content:
Here are the main points in 2-5 concise sentences:

January 9, 2024, Caroline County Board of Education meeting updates on Blueprint for Maryland's Future progress.
Assistant Superintendent Dr. Tara Downes said the district has received additional guidance from MSDE and AIB since spring 2023, allowing them to chunk tasks over a more manageable timeline.
Pillar chairs report progress: Pillar 1 chair Elizabeth Saylor (Early Childhood Education), Pillar 2 chair Dr. Rob Willoughby (High Quality and Diverse Teachers and Leaders), Lindsey McCormick (College and Career Readiness), Christal Harkowa (More Resources to Ensure All Students are Successful), Erica McDonald (Governance and Accountability).
Blueprint's objectives include increasing education funding, enriching student experiences, and accelerating student outcomes by 2026.

title: Moore says budget will balance, protect school funding
content: Gov. Wes Moore unveiled a $63.1 billion budget proposal on January 18, 2024, that balances the state's books and protects funding for Maryland public schools without raising taxes in the fiscal year starting July 1, 2024. The plan prioritizes public safety, affordable housing, child care, education, and public service. Moore crafted the budget with lawmakers, community leaders, and other stakeholders, aiming to make it a "reflection of our shared aspiration."

title: Talbot Board of Education discusses proposed budget, Blueprint's affects
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Talbot County Public Schools Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and CFO Sarah Jones presented the proposed fiscal year 2025 budget to the Talbot County Board of Education on January 19, 2024. The budget is $80.03 million with an increase of $7.98 million from the previous year due to adding 16 positions, meeting a Blueprint requirement for high-quality teachers, and increasing technology costs after COVID-19-related grants expire. Community school initiatives will also contribute to the budget increase. Possible reductions could save $259,000 without impacting student learning.

title: Superintendent shares schools' budget constraints with Commissioners
content: Caroline County Public Schools officials shared a $3.25 million surplus with the Caroline County Commissioners on January 16, 2024. The school district faces fiscal challenges due to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future unfunded mandate and declining pandemic-based grant funding in fiscal year 2025. Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons stated that support services salaries are not addressed in the Blueprint formula.

title: DCPS presentations show improvements in the district
content: Kindergarten readiness among Dorchester County kindergarteners increased by 7% from last school year, reaching 39%. DCPS director of curriculum, instruction and assessment Jodi Colman presented data on kindergarten readiness assessment results. The district saw an increase in students demonstrating readiness in language and literacy, mathematics, but a decrease in social foundations and physical well-being.

title: Student writes graphic novel about Frederick Douglass
content: Andrea C. Proimos, a recent Washington College graduate, wrote a graphic novel about traveling in the footsteps of Frederick Douglass. The graphic novel combines photographs and mixed media with her own art, following Douglass' life story from birth to escape. Proimos received a $3,000 Sophie Kerr Promise Grant to fund her research trip, which included visits to Baltimore, Rochester, New York, and Easton's farm fields.

title: Eastern Shore Delegation to ask governor for Cade formula restoration
content: The Eastern Shore Delegation voted to send a letter to Governor Wes Moore's office asking for restoration of the Cade Funding Formula in a supplemental budget, which would reduce $22 million in funding reductions proposed by the governor. The Cade formula, tying state funding to University System of Maryland institutions, would be reduced from 29% to 26.5%. Eastern Shore colleges, including Wor-Wic and Chesapeake Colleges, oppose the reduction due to its impact on student enrollment and budget sustainability.

title: Leonard Hall school closes after lease, maintenance issues arise
content: The Leonard Hall Junior Naval Academy in Leonardtown, MD, closed on January 30, 2024, after a lease termination decision by St. Mary's County commissioners. The school was paying $12,000 annually in rent and had maintenance issues estimated at $575,000, with the county requesting a financial sustainability plan by December 2023. Commissioner Mike Hewitt stated that the business plan for the school wasn't working, citing subsidizing private schools as not fair to public school funding. The commissioners voted to end the lease, but some supporters argued for continued operation and potential future reopening at another location.

title: Leonard Hall school closes after lease, maintenance issues arise
content: Leonard Hall Junior Naval Academy closed after lease termination by St. Mary's County commissioners due to maintenance issues and financial sustainability concerns. The school was paying $12,000 in annual rent, and its lease was set to expire June 30, but it closed last week. Headmistress Sarah Green submitted plans for a grant and repairs, which were deemed insufficient. Commissioner Mike Hewitt stated that subsidizing the cost of a private school is not in the best interest of all citizens.

title: Jennifer Stanley steps down from Oxford Kids Camp
content: Jennifer Stanley is stepping down after over 40 years as president and director of the Oxford Kids Camp in Oxford, Maryland. She leaves behind a legacy of the camp's growth from serving 50 kids to 250, with activities including swimming lessons, canoeing, and biking. Elizabeth Wainright has been named her replacement, who was a camper at age five and is being honored for taking over the tiller after Stanley steps down.

title: CarePacks awarded $15K from 100+ Women Who Care Talbot County
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

CarePacks of Talbot County received $15,000 from 100+ Women Who Care Talbot County on February 1, 2024. The group was founded by Emily Moody and Easton Mayor Megan Cook to provide meals and snacks to students with food insecurity. The organization aims to increase funding through membership donations, which currently stands at $300 per year.

title: CarePacks awarded $15K from 100+ Women Who Care Talbot County
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

CarePacks of Talbot County received $15,000 in funding from 100+ Women Who Care Talbot County, founded by Emily Moody and Easton Mayor Megan Cook. The program aims to provide nutrition support to Talbot County students who rely on school meals over weekends. The group has seen steady growth in membership since its inaugural meeting in September. Members can donate $300 per year, and the group meets quarterly to discuss funding for local nonprofits.

title: Jennifer Stanley steps down from Oxford Kids Camp
content: Jennifer Stanley steps down as founder and director of Oxford Kids Camp after over 40 years, leaving behind a legacy in the community. She established the camp with a focus on biking, nature, and outdoor activities in 1982, serving up to 250 kids per week. Stanley's successor is Elizabeth Wainwright, who has been part of the camp since she was a camper at age five.

title: Teacher, Support Staff of the Year nominations now open
content: Talbot County Public Schools has begun accepting nominations for Teacher of the Year and Support Staff of the Year awards. The deadline is February 9, 2024. Eligible candidates include teachers with state certification and six years of exemplary teaching experience, as well as full-time support staff employees who have worked for at least two years. Dr. Helga Einhorn, Assistant Superintendent for Teaching, Learning & Leading, will oversee the selection process.

title: Sense of urgency needed on school absenteeism
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maryland lawmakers and educators met to discuss chronic absenteeism, with data showing over one-third of Maryland K-12 students missed 10% or more school days last year.
