Nearly 35% of kindergarten students statewide are chronically absent. Gov. Wes Moore has expressed concern about the issue, which can impact test scores, grades, and a child's ability to graduate. A task force will study chronic absenteeism in Maryland's public schools, with a report due by Dec. 1. Maryland Board of Education President Clarence Crawford notes that chronic absenteeism can have long-lasting, serious consequences for students throughout their lives.

title: House GOP introduces bill to repeal Biden college plan
content: The House Committee on Education and the Workforce has advanced a Republican-sponsored bill repealing key aspects of President Joe Biden's plans to make college more affordable, including the College Cost Reduction Act introduced by Rep. Virginia Foxx (R-North Carolina). The measure passed on a party-line 22-19 vote, with Democrats offering amendments that were defeated. The bill aims to establish a streamlined data system and create a performance-based grant program, while repealing Biden administration regulations aimed at protecting student borrowers.

title: Caroline students sign apprenticeship agreements
content: Caroline County Public Schools signed four youth apprenticeship agreements with local businesses: three in the Technology Department and one in the Chesapeake Culinary Arts Center. The students involved are Evamarie Vargas Villacorta, Dana Velasquez-Cifuentes, Lawrence Johnson, and Wilson Clough. CCPS Superintendent Dr. Derek Simmons led the signing, which he described as an "exciting day" made possible by former Assistant Superintendent Milton Nagel's vision. Representatives from the Maryland State Department of Education attended to support the program.

title: DCPS announces teacher awards finalists
content: Dorchester County Public Schools announced finalists for Teacher of the Year and First Class Teacher of the Year for the 2024-2025 school year. The finalists include Emma Brant, Jennifer Filopovic, Katelyn Robinson, Christy Starling, Christie Carels, Colleen Carney, Anthony Thomas, Kaylen Trice, Kierra Farrare, Crystal Carpenter, Jordan Lewis, Devyn Thompson, Haley Wright, Brianna Sann. Winners will be announced at a reception on March 26, 2024.

title: New Fellowship of Christian Athletes club unites and inspires students
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

A new Fellowship of Christian Athletes club was established at Centreville Middle School in Queen Anne's County, Maryland, uniting students with inspirational music and fellowship activities. Jeff Simmons, area director of FCA for Queen Anne's and Talbot counties, oversees the club alongside teacher Thomas Hayman, who is dedicated to teaching and investing in his students. The FCA has been active globally for over 60 years and currently has 20,000 huddle meetings worldwide, including 115 countries. Simmons has raised the entire budget for the Queen Anne's and Talbot counties region through community support, with some schools still without an FCA presence.

title: Talbot Board of Education passes FY2025 budget
content: The Talbot County Public Schools Board of Education approved the FY2025 budget, which increases the unrestricted operating budget by $7.9 million to $79.9 million. The district is seeking a 3.4% increase due to decreased federal funding and losing $4.8 million in COVID-19 related grant funding. A proposed capital budget of $12.1 million includes renovations, installations, and replacements at various schools.

title: TCPS gives Blueprint updates
content: The Talbot County Board of Education meeting shared updates on the Blueprint for Maryland's Future plan. The Maryland State Department of Education has approved the College and Career Readiness Standard. Helga Einhorn presented two options for students to be considered college and career ready: earning a high school GPA of 3.0 or scoring proficient or above in Algebra I and English Language Arts. The new standard goes into effect immediately, with an interim standard remaining in place until July 1, 2025.

title: Corporate tax breaks end up costing schools
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Kansas City, Missouri's school district lost $237.3 million between 2017 and 2023 due to property tax breaks granted to companies. An estimated 95% of U.S. cities provide similar economic development tax incentives, diverting billions from large urban school districts and small suburban/rural districts. A three-month investigation found that tax abatements disproportionately harm schools serving low-income and racial minority students, leading to funding gaps, delayed maintenance, and teacher shortages.

title: Free young gardeners event at library
content: The Talbot County Garden Club and Talbot County Free Library will host "The Young Gardeners: Flower and Plant Press Project" on March 7 at the downtown library for kids in grades 1-4 from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. The event is free, free registration is required at tcfl.org or 410-822-1626, and is hosted by the Talbot County Garden Club's Young Gardeners Committee.

title: Anti-war protests, rises in antisemitism magnify challenges for free speech on college campuses
content: Anti-war protests and rising antisemitism are raising challenges for free speech on college campuses, with universities facing debates over balancing protected speech with safety and harassment concerns. The Anti-Defamation League reports a rise in antisemitism since Oct. 7, while the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression argues that students' First Amendment rights are being restricted. The U.S. Department of Education is investigating Title VI violations at over 40 colleges, including Johns Hopkins University, Harvard University, and the University of Michigan. Shira Goodman and Jane Kirtley express concerns about government and donor influence on speech, with potential blowback for free expression.

title: KCPS calendar approved with post Labor Day start
content: The Kent County Board of Education approved a calendar for the 2024-25 school year with a post-Labor Day start. The new calendar includes 180 instruction days and two inclement weather days. It begins on Tuesday, Sept. 3, with staggered starts for different grade levels, including: first through sixth grades and ninth-graders (Sept. 3), 10th, 11th, and 12th grades (Sept. 4), and pre-kindergartners and kindergartners (Sept. 5).

title: Wright named North Caroline assistant principal
content: Dr. Derek Simmons announced Chastity Wright's appointment as assistant principal of North Caroline High School at the February 6 Board of Education meeting. Wright has been dean of students since the start of the school year and was chosen unanimously by an interview committee in 2012.

title: Dorchester superintendent stepping down March 1
content: Dorchester County Public Schools Superintendent David Bromwell will step down effective March 1, with his term ending June 30. The Dorchester County Board of Education has announced that they will vote on an interim superintendent at their next meeting.

title: School board adopts 2024-2025 calendar
content: The Caroline County Public Schools Board of Education voted unanimously to adopt a new school year calendar for the 2024-2025 school year, starting on Wednesday, August 28. Dr. Derek Simmons presented two alternatives, which were favored by 70% of staff and 75% of parents who responded to a survey, with the pre-Labor Day start being adopted. The calendar also includes winter break starting December 20 with a half-day Friday and students returning to school on January 7.

title: Thompson voted interim DCPS superintendent
content: Jymil Thompson was appointed as interim superintendent of Dorchester County Public Schools, effective March 1, 2024. Thompson has been assistant superintendent since September 2023 and previously served in various roles at Mace's Lane Middle School from 2017 to 2020. The decision comes after David Bromwell, who was appointed as superintendent in 2020, stepped down from his position due to a mutually decided departure. A search for a new superintendent will begin on July 1, 2024.

title: Responsible Fathers Initiative empowers, strengthens men
content: The Responsible Fathers Initiative, founded by Corey Pack in 2019, is a local nonprofit that empowers men to become better fathers through evidence-based fatherhood programs and resources. The initiative uses curriculum developed by the National Fatherhood Initiative and has grown to include three in-person groups inside the Talbot County Detention Center and several community-based groups in Easton and Cambridge. Pack's inspiration came from seeing the negative impact of absent or irresponsible fathers on families, particularly children born into households without a responsible father figure. The initiative has partnered with organizations such as the Neighborhood Service Center to provide wraparound services, including housing, transportation, food, and financial literacy assistance.

title: Early learners meet with success at Kinder Connection
content: Kinder Connection, a licensed child care home in Betterton, MD, opened last summer with a focus on neurodivergent children and play-based learning. Owners Elizabeth and James Greenwell expanded their program after just under a year, planning to add 600 square feet to serve more children. The center participates in MSDE-approved programs, including ASPIRE Pre-K, and offers field trips for families. Kinder Connection accepts children through the ASPIRE program and Child Care Scholarships; they run a summer camp as well.

title: 'Teaching & Transformation: Semester in the Chesapeake Classroom'
content: Washington College's Center for Environment and Society announces the grand opening of MuSE: A Community Museum in Chestertown, Maryland, with a rotating exhibit "Teaching & Transformation: Semester in the Chesapeake Classroom" showcasing Washington College students' projects on the Chesapeake Bay region. The museum is located at 210 S. Cross Street. The exhibit, which analyzes solutions to environmental problems and explores the nexus between science, policy, and people's everyday lives, will remain open through August 2024.

title: Books rife with sexual content
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article in 2-5 sentences:

Maryland's "Freedom to Read" Act (SB 0738), passed last fall, has made several books with graphic sexual content available to students without parental knowledge or consent. The Carroll County Board had previously removed these books due to complaints from parents, which included young elementary school children. Books on the list include the autobiography of Jaycee Dugard and books featuring explicit descriptions of sex, rape scenes, and child experimentation. Some Maryland schools are struggling with basic literacy while being exposed to such content. The Talbot County Republican Central Committee has questioned the agenda behind ignoring parents' wishes.

title: Dyer achieves Eagle Scout
content: Vincent Thomas Dyer achieved Eagle Scout status on March 7, 2024, at the Scout House in St. Michaels. He earned 26 merit badges and completed a final project raising $2,000 to honor veterans in Cordova. His family, politicians, civic leaders, and Boy Scouts attended the ceremony, where he received the Eagle Scout badge and neckerchief from his parents, Paul and Kimberly Dyer.

title: Chesapeake College's Hispanic/Latino Student Union provides community, support
content: Chesapeake College's Hispanic/Latino Student Union was established by Zulema Delacruz Martinez and LaSella Hall to provide community and support for the school's growing Latino student population. The union hosted a FAFSA assistance night in February 2024, where over 90% of attendees applied for financial aid. LaSella Hall developed the "Hall Method," which focuses on empowering students through hard conversations and advocating for their voices. Zulema Delacruz Martinez aims to spread the message that higher education is reachable for immigrant families and plans to run her own nonprofit organization.

title: The Navy’s 'best kept secret'
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The U.S. Naval Sea Cadet Corps, established in 1958 by the Secretary of the Navy, has 380 units and 9,000 enrolled members. The program for young men and women aged 10 to 18 aims to instill values of discipline, accountability, and teamwork, preparing them to be productive citizens and future leaders. The Maryland Division's unit, formed in April 2018, has grown from five cadets to 29, with a focus on promoting patriotism and community service. Lt. Maryjoe Phillips is a driving force behind the program, which is supported by the U.S. Navy and Coast Guard.

title: Student building projects impress judges
content: A Wicomico County Public Schools team won the gold cup in the architecture, construction and engineering competition at Sts. Peter and Paul High School on March 10, 2024. The winning project was a Salisbury Riverfront Community Center. Judge James Cook praised the industry, stating he was "blown away" by the projects. The event was sponsored by various companies and organizations, including ACE Mentors, Easton Utilities, DBF/ACE Gerald Friedel Legacy, and others.

title: No one knows how to pay for Maryland's massive education reform
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maryland's Democratic-led legislature passed the Blueprint for Maryland's Future in 2021, aiming to pour billions into public schools, but didn't outline long-term funding plans. The General Assembly will start running a structural deficit by fiscal year 2025, growing nearly sixfold by fiscal year 2029, and estimating over $4 billion in costs by then. State officials have offered various solutions, including raising taxes or cutting back on the Blueprint's demands, but no consensus has been reached. Governor Wes Moore and Democrats support the current plan, while Republicans advocate for a "Blueprint lite" approach. The Accountability and Implementation Board is expected to issue recommendations regarding the budget challenges.

title: Local student wins national essay contest
content: Viana Johnston, an eighth-grade student at Lighthouse Christian Academy in Stevensville, won the national middle school winner of a Bill of Rights Essay contest hosted by the Stanley M. Herzog Foundation in 2023. The contest was part of the foundation's program to advance Christian education. Viana received $250 and her school $250 as prize money. Her essay emphasized the significance of the Bill of Rights, ratified on December 15, 1791.

title: Target team will not see expansion this season
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Kent Island Clay Target Team will not see expansion this season due to affiliation risks and litigation concerns. Superintendent Patricia Saelens noted that Queen Anne's County was the only public school district in Maryland offering clay target teams, but will keep the team limit as it is for now. The team, which is self-funded and participates at a private facility, currently has six all-volunteer coaches and has seen growing interest in the sport. Shawn Connolly, head coach of the team, had requested approval to expand the student limit, but was denied by the board.

title: Get a sneak peak at Chesapeake Forum's spring lineup
content: Chesapeake Forum will unveil its Spring 2024 class lineup at the Academy Art Museum in Easton on April 3, from 3:30 to 5 p.m. Registration for classes starts April 4 and begins on April 11. The organization's "Lectures on the Shore" speaker series returns on May 9 with a presentation about the Fine family of award-winning filmmakers. Chesapeake Forum is based in Easton, MD, and offers more than 30 classes this spring covering various topics including birding, car maintenance, and history.

title: TCPS looks into creation of clay target shooting club
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 sentences:

Talbot County Board of Education heard from five public members supporting the creation of a high school clay target shooting club. The district's Chief Financial Officer Sarah Jones reported that research into the feasibility of the club was ongoing, with concerns about financial liability and risk management. Talbot Rod & Gun Club President Joe Capozzoli spoke at a previous board meeting in October requesting approval for the club. A discussion on the topic was held at a February MABE meeting, and an annual meeting is scheduled for late April to vote on the matter. The district expects to have answers by May, with Board President Emily Jackson stating that MABE's decision would determine the board's ability to approve the club creation.

title: Jymil Thompson resigns from Talbot County Board of Education
content: Jymil Thompson resigned from his seat on the Talbot County Board of Education due to appointment as interim superintendent of Dorchester County Public Schools. He was appointed in March after serving as assistant superintendent for DCPS since September 2023. Thompson's term on the board ended in December 2022, but he will serve until 2026 as interim superintendent.

title: Rotary event encourages students to explore local jobs, careers
content: Local Rotary Clubs sponsored Career Day at Chesapeake College in Wye Mills, MD on March 15, 2024, for high school students from Queen Anne's County High, Kent Island High and Wye River Upper School. Doug Storck of the Centreville Rotary Club partnered with Chesapeake College to host the event, which included one-on-one learning opportunities, mock interviews, financial guidance workshops, a career fair with 30 local businesses, and guest speaker Dale Walls from Corsica Technologies.

title: Maryland teachers learn from success in literacy labs
content:
Maryland educators gathered at Cecil County School of Technology for a Literacy Learning Lab hosted by Cecil County Public Schools.
The lab took place in March 2024 and brought together educators from 24 school districts to learn about CCPS's methodologies for identifying student literacy needs.
CCPS uses the Bookworms program, which provides resources for reading and writing courses, in conjunction with assessments to make data-driven decisions.
The county was identified as third in state performance on reading and writing assessments.
Cecil County Public Schools has led the state in meeting requirements of the 2019 Ready to Read Act.

title: Maryland’s teacher shortage: Will the Blueprint’s plan for better pay, training do enough?
content:
Maryland's teacher shortage worsened to 28 subjects in the current school year, with gaps in English as a second language, health science, and special education. The Blueprint for Maryland's Future aims to address the shortage through higher pay ($60,000 by 2026), better training, and recruitment efforts.

However, experts like Simon Birenbaum and Mike Hansen question whether higher pay alone will solve the issue, citing the need for more effective recruitment and retention strategies.

The teacher shortage is partly due to declining interest in teaching careers, with fewer people enrolling in teacher preparation programs since 2012. Maryland's issuance of conditional certificates also rose between 2018-2022, leading to an influx of less-credentialed teachers.

The Blueprint also aims to boost diversity and improve career prospects for teachers, but concerns remain about the effectiveness of these measures.

title: College students travel to every Easton in US
content: Three Lafayette College students and a recent alumna visited all 21 incorporated Eastons in the US, traveling by single-engine airplane to reach towns in Pennsylvania, Illinois, Kansas, Missouri, Texas, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, and New York, before arriving at Easton, Maryland on March 24, 2024. The group met with local guides, including Mayor Megan Cook, and collected souvenirs while keeping a low weight due to air travel regulations. They received financial support from an alumnus and covered some of their own expenses. The trip was part of an academic project and personal adventure, lasting around 10 days.

title: Foundation of HOPE leading girls to success
content: Keasha Haythe founded the Foundation of HOPE in Easton, MD, an after-school program for middle school girls on the Eastern Shore that began eight years ago. The program aims to provide cultural, social, spiritual and educational development to help young girls lead productive lives in their communities. John Englehart, assistant manager of human resources for Easton Utilities, led a presentation to the cohort of girls on marketing themselves and achieving career goals. The program covers topics such as low self-esteem, bullying, financial literacy, and workforce development.

title: Board of Education Member Donna DiGiacomo resigns
content: Donna DiGiacomo resigns from Caroline County Board of Education after three years and four months citing concerns over Superintendent Derek Simmons' use of the term "minions" to describe employees during a March 5 meeting. DiGiacomo had emailed her resignation to Maryland Superintendent of Education on Monday, March 25, 2024. Her term was set to end November 30, 2024.

title: Dorchester County awards Teacher of the Year to Katelyn Robinson
content: Katelyn Robinson, a second-grade teacher at Maple Elementary School in East New Market, Maryland, was named Teacher of the Year by Dorchester County Public Schools on March 27, 2024. Katelyn's peers and friends were in attendance as she received the award. Jordan Lewis, a Choptank Elementary School teacher, and Haley Wright, a Maple Elementary School teacher, were also recognized as winners of the First Class Teacher of the Year award for their first year of teaching.

title: WKHS celebrates 50 years of student public radio
content: WKHS celebrated its 50 years of student public radio on March 28, 1974, with a format of educational and public affairs programming, starting with Elton John's "Rocket Man." The station has been managed by Chris Singleton since 2008, who attributes the program's success to his predecessor, Ken Collins, and superintendent Dr. Karen Couch, who supported the program in 2013. The station has undergone several upgrades, including a $160,000 remodel in 2018, and will host a Tune Fest celebration on May 4 with live music and local food trucks.

title: WKHS celebrates 50 years of student public radio
content: WKHS student public radio celebrates its 50th anniversary with a live on-air broadcast, marking the first of four instructional periods at the station. The program was founded in 1974 and has been led by current station manager Chris Singleton since 2008. WKHS has undergone significant upgrades, including a $160,000 infrastructure upgrade in 2018, to maintain its relevance in today's digital age. A 50th anniversary celebration, called Tune Fest, is set to take place on May 4 at Red Acres Farm in Worton.

title: Students embrace history once again in regional competition
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 sentences:

Nearly 200 students from Caroline, Cecil, Queen Anne's and Talbot counties participated in the annual regional history day event at Chesapeake College on March 23. The event was organized by Thomas Hayman and part of the national National History Day program. Students submitted projects in five categories: Paper, Website, Performance, Documentary, and Exhibit, with winners invited to compete in the Maryland statewide competition. The event has grown since its inception as an after-school program, with two area students going on to compete in the national event in recent years. Over 50 awards were given out to students, including several first-place finishes and Best in Region awards.

title: DCPS enters agreement to increase professional development for adminstration
content: Dorchester County Public Schools approved a purchasing agreement with Creative Leadership Solutions to provide coaching and professional development support for administrators. Interim Superintendent Jymil Thompson stated that the district aims to improve tier one instruction over a three-year period through training of staff and leadership. The funding for the $138,000 services will come from Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief III funding.

title: Raskin speech at University of Maryland disrupted by protesters
content: Maryland Rep. Jamie Raskin's planned lecture on democracy at the University of Maryland was disrupted by pro-Palestinian protesters on April 2, 2024. Protesters shouted that Raskin is "complicit in genocide," while Raskin emphasized his support for a two-state solution and ceasefire. The incident led to Raskin abandoning his speech and responding to questions from the audience, with University President Darryll Pines later terminating the lecture early.

title: Megan Borga is teacher of the year
content: Megan Borga, a fifth-grade teacher at Kennard Elementary School in Queen Anne's County, MD, was named the 2024 Queen Anne's County Public Schools' Teacher of the Year. She was selected during the annual awards gala held in March. Borga received the honor from Superintendent Dr. Patricia Saelens and expressed gratitude to her family, friends, coworkers, principal, and the selection committee for their support.

title: Talibah Chikwendu appointed to Dorchester Board of Education
content: Talibah Chikwendu has been appointed by the Dorchester County Council to fill the vacant seat on the District 2 Dorchester County Board of Education, which ends in 2026. The appointment was made due to Theresa Stafford's passing, who served from 2022 until her death in mid-December. Chikwendu is a graduate of Dorchester County Public Schools and has worked as a school librarian for 10 years and a high school teacher for the past five years. She aims to serve the community and bring value through transparency and acclimating herself to district needs, amidst budget season.

title: Rice named new Echo Hill executive director
content: Peter P. Rice III has been appointed as the new executive director of Echo Hill Outdoor School in Worton, Maryland. He was previously an integral part of the school's team since 2014 and will serve as the second executive director in the organization's history. Rice succeeds his father, Peter Rice Jr., who led the institution for 51 years until his recent retirement. The new executive director brings a wealth of experience in outdoor education, event management, and strategic planning to the role.

title: Country School students experience solar eclipse
content: Country School students witnessed a partial solar eclipse on April 9, 2024, with the moon blocking out nearly 90% of the sun. The event occurred in Easton, MD, and was part of a rare celestial occurrence that won't be visible over the continental US for another 20 years. Teachers prepared students about eclipse viewing safety and science behind an eclipse.

title: 'I am speechless:' TCPS awards teacher, support staff of the year
content: Rosario Steele was awarded Talbot County Public Schools Support Staff of the Year in 2024-2025, along with Jeremy Hillyard, who won the district's Teacher of the Year honor. Hillyard has taught at Easton High School since 2010 and is working to create a mentorship program for Hispanic students. Steele works as an instructional assistant for English as a second language students at EHS.

title: Women to Watch event recognizes more than 200 local leaders
content: More than 200 women from the Mid-Shore region were nominated for the annual Women to Watch magazine, with 16 selected by the committee to be featured in this year's issue. The event was held at The Avalon Theatre in Easton on April 14, 2024, and honored local leaders such as Ivette Furneisen (lawyer), Sharon Pepukayi (superintendent of Talbot County Public Schools), and Meisha Amia (nurse, author, and entrepreneur). The Women to Watch magazine aims to highlight impactful work being done by women in the Mid-Shore community.

title: Chesapeake College shapes Eastern Shore's future
content: Chesapeake College launched a new brand this academic year, highlighting its role in preparing students for "what's next." The college empowers individuals with skills to succeed, strengthening local economic growth and creating pathways to prosperity. Chesapeake College collaborates with partners, including K-12 education, four-year institutions, and businesses, to create curricula that resonate with real-world demands. The college boasts a 100% pass rate in its nursing program and has expanded trades offerings, including an advanced manufacturing program. Enrollment is up 9.5% this year.

title: Beyond Words brings creative and innovative opportunities to the Shore
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Lindsey Parte, a special education teacher, has launched Beyond Words Tutoring in Stevensville, Maryland. The business offers innovative services including a hybrid homeschooling program, virtual dyslexia tutoring, academic summer camps, and non-attorney special education advocate services. The hybrid program, open to students ages 6-11, focuses on math and reading with a creative and child-led approach. Virtual dyslexia tutoring is available for students ages 6-high school, while the academic summer camp (July 29-Aug. 16) aims to prevent educational regression. Non-attorney special education advocate services are also offered to empower parents in the IEP process.

title: No primary election to be held for Caroline County Board of Education seats
content: Caroline County's Board of Education District 2 will be decided in the 2024 General Election, skipping a primary election due to fewer than three candidates filing for candidacy. Stefanie Johnson is the sole candidate running under the committee "Stefanie Johnson for Caroline BOE". The general election is set for November 5, 2024, allowing residents to vote in person or by mail.

title: Dorchester Board of Education hears security update
content: Dorchester County Public Schools reported a decrease in student fighting (25% down) but an increase in adult attacks on students (22%), adult threats (15%) and bullying incidents (19%). Michael Richardson, DCPS School Security and Emergency Management Manager, presented the update to the board, highlighting safety and security improvements. The district has implemented additional cameras, drug test kits, updated emergency procedures, and is working on security vestibules for elementary schools and mass notification systems for select campuses.

title: Students speak of freedom in essay contest
content: Proud parents gathered at C. Henry Price II, American Legion Post 246 in Betterton on April 19 to congratulate their children during an Americanism Essay Award Reception for third, fourth, and fifth graders of Galena Elementary. The winners, Chace Foye, Athena Stone, and Carter Carroll, received cash awards ($50, $25, and $10 respectively) for their essays on what freedom means to them. The event was organized by the Auxiliary at the Legion, with Betterton Mayor Donald Sutton in attendance.

title: School board looks at changing name of school bearing name of Revolutionary War general, former governor who owned slaves
content: The Charles County Board of Education reviewed changing the name of General Smallwood Middle School due to concerns over Gen. William Smallwood's ownership of slaves. Gen. Smallwood was born in 1732 and served as a delegate and governor before joining the Revolutionary War effort. The school system plans to survey the community from May to early June and consider costs for renaming, which could range from $64,500 to $124,500. The Charles County Board of Education will gather feedback on potential name changes in June.

title: Chesapeake Multicultural after-school program lets students learn through taste
content: Fourth and fifth graders in the Chesapeake Multicultural Resource Center After-school Program visited Bonheur Ice Cream and Pie in Easton on April 28, 2024, to learn about the profession of sweets-making from local chefs Estela-Vianney Ramirez and Tyler Heim. The program focuses on STEM education, reading skills, nutrition, and community engagement for Hispanic elementary school students in Talbot County. Ramírez has worked with the program for over a decade, while chef Harley Peet shared ideas for new flavors during the tour. Students received a scoop of ice cream and toppings to create their own flavor at the end of the visit.

title: Job opportunities, money available for graduates
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maryland's Department of Service and Civic Innovation offers job opportunities for graduating high school seniors or former graduates with a minimum salary of $15/hour and health insurance. The program requires host sites to sign up by May 1, but youth can apply later in May. State delegates and senators also offer financial aid to students through the Commission on Higher Education (mhec.maryland.gov). Unfortunately, many resources go unclaimed due to lack of awareness or motivation among applicants.

title: Candidates compete for 3 open Dorchester Board of Education seats
content:
Here is a summary of the candidates running for the Dorchester County Board of Education:

**District 1:**

* Brandy Dawson Cumberland: Fresh perspective as parent and invested community member with experience in quality initiative projects.
* Brandy's goals include prioritizing safety, transparency, learning, retaining quality educators, and accountability.

**District 5:**

* Chris Wheedleton (current board member): Alignment on a strategic plan to improve and grow the district, with focus on academic success, partnerships, school safety, workforce, and operational efficiency.
* Chris supports the county handling Blueprint in an honest and open way, sharing successes and challenges with stakeholders.

**District 1:**

* Brandy Dawson Cumberland: Added value through developing the publicly available Data Dashboard and connecting it to the business community, reinstating a CASE Agricultural program at DCTC.

Note: Jerome Harris did not respond to candidate questions in time for publication.

title: Two face off for District 3 Dorchester County Board of Education position
content:
Christine LaMonica is running for the District 3 Dorchester County Board of Education seat.
She wants to address safety concerns in schools and advocate for quality education for all students.
LaMonica believes the board needs to promote transparency and collaboration in decision-making and work towards common goals with open communication and respect.

Susan Morgan, current Vice President, is also running for the District 3 position.
Morgan's top priority is raising academic performance, particularly in reading and math.
She wants to improve kindergarten readiness programs and reduce chronic absenteeism.

title: Three candidates compete for District 5 Dorchester Board of Education seat
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Three candidates are running for the District 5 Dorchester County Board of Education seat: Chris Wheedleton, Mike Hartford, and Jerome Harris. 
Chris Wheedleton has been serving as a board member and focuses on addressing the need for clear direction and accountability in the school district. 
Mike Hartford aims to bring transparency and involve parents in decision-making processes.
Kindergarten readiness among Dorchester County kindergarteners is at 39% this school year compared to 32% the previous year, according to DCPS data.

title: Talbot schools recognize community partners
content: Talbot County Public School District recognized over 100 community partners at a breakfast event on April 26, 2024, in Easton, Maryland. The district chose various organizations and individuals to honor for their support throughout the year. Notable recipients included the Talbot County Public Library, Rack Room Shoes, Second Chance Thrift Shop, Foundation of Hope, and the St. Michaels Fire Department.

title: Three vie for District 1 Dorchester County Board of Education seat
content:
**Board of Education Candidates:**

* The board needs to prioritize transparent leadership and engagement by establishing clear channels of communication, soliciting feedback, collaborating with community partners, and prioritizing school safety.
* Goals include improving academic outcomes, fostering parent and community involvement, addressing chronic absenteeism and discipline issues, and promoting college and career readiness.
* The county should fully fund the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, including increasing teacher pay and partnering with Historically Black Colleges and Universities to support diverse teachers and leaders.

**Dorchester County Public Schools:**

* Kindergarten readiness has increased from 32% to 39%, indicating progress but still needing improvement.
* Strategies to build on this progress include expanding access to high-quality pre-K, increasing parent and community engagement, providing professional development for early childhood educators, and implementing evidence-based practices proven to enhance school readiness.

title: Benedictine hosts ribbon-cutting and groundbreaking
content:
Scott Evans, executive director of Benedictine School, led a ribbon-cutting ceremony for a new road and a groundbreaking for new student residences at Ridgely's school property, where $3 million was secured from the U.S. Senate, state legislature, and community development block grants.

Benedictine received $1.8 million in congressional directed funding to support new spaces for residents with developmental and intellectual disabilities and autism. The new residential wings will include recreational areas, dining space, and an infirmary.

Benedictine School is launching its 'Transforming Lives' campaign to address the needs of its student demographic, which has changed since existing residential spaces were built, particularly due to the increase in students with complicated forms of autism.

title: Candidates to face off for Talbot Board of Education positions
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Candidates for Talbot County Board of Education positions include CANDACE HENRY, CYNTHIA JURRIUS, ANNA HOWIE, and others. They will compete in the May 14 primary election for Districts 2, 5, and 6. The board members will serve four-year terms starting December 1, 2024, and ending December 1, 2028.

The candidates discuss issues such as teacher recruitment, retention, diversity, equity, and access to education. They also address the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, providing exceptional education opportunities while being fiscally responsible.

CANDACE HENRY supports creating a welcoming environment for educators, increasing funding for high-quality early childhood programs, and addressing the opportunity gap. CYNTHIA JURRIUS emphasizes student mastery of essential knowledge and skills, positive school climate, and family engagement.

ANNA HOWIE focuses on providing exceptional education opportunities while being fiscally responsible, utilizing grants to improve instructional materials, and ensuring teacher compensation respects their professional position.

title: St. Michaels library looks to expand its footprint
content: The Talbot County Free Library St. Michaels Branch plans a 3,700-square-foot expansion to be completed by December 2025 or January 2026. The library has raised $5 million and is seeking an additional $500,000 through a private fundraising campaign. Architects Davis, Bowen and Friedel are working on the project. Representatives have engaged with community members in town-hall meetings to determine the needs of the new library, which will include quiet spaces for reading, improved facilities for teens, and interactive outside spaces.

title: HopStart learners making world a better place
content: The 24th annual HopStart new venture awards program at Johns Hopkins University took place on a date in May 2024. Hosted by the Center for Leadership Education at Johns Hopkins, the event challenged Hopkins students to develop innovative business plans and pitch them to a diverse panel of judges. The event included alumni such as Len Foxwell, who is an integral member of the Hopkins team that plans and executes HopStart, and featured programs in two categories: general ventures and medical technology/life science ventures. The program received 50 submissions with ideas ranging from leveraging internet use for agriculture to simplifying credential verification processes for medical care providers.

title: Moms For Liberty fields candidates in elections
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

Moms For Liberty backs candidates Ann C. O'Connor, Karla Wieland-Cherry, and Kerry Gunshenan in Talbot County Board of Education elections. The group has been accused of promoting anti-LGBTQ+ misinformation and fighting to scrub diverse material from lesson plans. Three candidates submitted questionnaires with no answers, sparking concern among voters. A November election will give candidates another opportunity to share their stances on issues. Talbot County recently celebrated the business community's economic development efforts and addressed rising sea levels along the Gulf coast.

title: Maryland’s education ‘Blueprint’ struggles to expand pre-K
content: Maryland's pre-K program struggles to expand due to a lack of private providers and inadequate physical space in schools. The state's "Blueprint" plan aims to make pre-K free for low- and moderate-income families and available to all 3- and 4-year-olds, but faces challenges in finding enough private providers. Many districts are struggling to meet the requirement of having 35% of pre-K seats filled by private providers, and some child care centers lack the necessary funding and space to participate. The state's physical space requirements for pre-K classrooms have also been criticized as too inflexible.

title: Elkton teacher has green thumb for growing students' knowledge
content: Brittany Rigdon is the 2024 Cecil County Teacher of the Year, announced by Cecil County Public Schools officials last month. She has taught horticulture at the Cecil County School of Technology for 16 years and is known for her vast knowledge of horticulture and ability to effectively teach students. Rigdon's students praise her teaching style, saying she "likes to get on our level" and makes complex subjects understandable. She encourages her students to set goals in areas beyond academics, including career and personal life.

title: Will plan for better pay ease teacher shortage?
content: Maryland is struggling with a teacher shortage, with 28 subjects short of teachers as of the current school year, up from 17 five years earlier. The state's Blueprint for Maryland's Future aims to address the issue through higher pay, better training, and stronger recruitment efforts, increasing teacher pay to $60,000 by 2026. However, experts and educators have mixed views on whether this will effectively address the root causes of the shortage.

title: School officials: Blueprint money is not enough
content:
School officials in Maryland's 24 school districts cited insufficient funding under the state's Blueprint for Maryland's Future plan, which aims to rebuild public schools. The Blueprint provides $16.6 billion over 2024-2029 and billions more after that, but local district leaders said it is not enough. By 2034, local districts will need to pay $700 million more annually under the Blueprint's formulas.

The Maryland Association of Counties listed concerns about unfunded mandates, including construction costs, staffing, data systems, student support, and transportation. County officials, such as Harford County Executive Bob Cassilly, say the Blueprint is unaffordable.

Local districts face challenges in implementing the Blueprint's requirements, including shifting resources to higher-need schools and increasing funding for pre-K and teacher salaries. The state project that 15 of the 24 school districts will need to increase local funding levels before the Blueprint rollout is complete by 2034.

The Maryland Association of Counties listed a litany of concerns about the Blueprint's cost estimates, including increased spending on construction costs, staffing, and transportation. County officials have refused to increase school funding above state requirements, leading to $9 million cash shortfalls in some districts.

title: Dr. Toughlove’s Book Club
content: Dr. Toughlove endorses Andrea Beaty's children's books, including "Aaron Slater, Illustrator", which tells the story of a boy struggling to learn to write but discovering his artistic talent instead. The book is part of Beaty and illustrator David Roberts' series, also featuring "Iggy Peck, Architect", "Rosie Revere, Engineer", and others. Dr. Toughlove recommends the book for children aged 4-7 and notes that it includes downloadable coloring sheets on Andrea Beaty's website.

title: It's time to learn from history and speak out
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

College campus protestors are not anti-war protesters but rabidly antisemitic supporters of Hamas. They reject Israel's right to exist and defend actions that include verbal harassment, threats, and physical harm against Jews and Jewish students. Public officials and college administrators should share Martin Niemöller's story of inaction leading to persecution during WWII to acknowledge the dangers of antisemitism. David Reel writes that learning from history is crucial to avoid repeating it, warning that silence or indifference to hatred can lead to devastating consequences.

title: Maple Elementary School celebrates Teacher Appreciation Week
content: Maple Elementary School in Cambridge, MD celebrated Teacher Appreciation Week from May 7-11, 2024. Principal Myyesha Ford planned activities to boost staff morale and show appreciation for teachers. Activities included a "Survivor"-themed challenge wheel, team-building exercises, and anonymous praise messages. Teachers Haley Wright and Natalie Drake praised the event, highlighting their enjoyment of feeling seen and appreciated by colleagues and administrators.

title: Blatant attack on character
content: Karla Wieland-Cherry is running for Talbot County Board of Education District 5. The Star Democrat has attacked her character, claiming she was endorsed by Moms for Liberty without being prepared to answer questions. Karla had previously stated she was seeking input from parents and finishing college courses before campaigning in June. She accused the newspaper's editor, Jim Johnson, of biased hatred. The controversy began after Karla shared her views on Facebook.

title: Quality child care is a collective responsibility
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 3 concise sentences:

Many Republican leaders at the state level recognize and are addressing the child care crisis through funding fixes such as grants and tax credits. However, at the national level, their party remains a roadblock to meaningful solutions. The alternative approach, advocated by many European countries, recognizes high-quality care as a collective responsibility, enshrining it as a human right that values the well-being of all individuals regardless of socio-economic status.

title: Moms For Liberty advocates for school parents
content:
Here is a summary of the article:

Moms For Liberty Talbot chapter chair Jan Greenhawk responds to an article by Executive Editor Jim Johnson stating that her group supports candidates in local school board elections. Greenhawk corrects Johnson, saying Moms For Liberty did not endorse any candidates and has not raised questions across the country. She disputes the accuracy of Johnson's portrayal of the group, citing biased allegations from The Associated Press and a liberal professor. Greenhawk emphasizes the group's dedication to parental rights and positive dialogue with local education officials, including Superintendent Dr. Pepukayi and school board President Emily Jackson.

title: Demand proficiency at all grades
content: Moms for Liberty (M4L) was formed in Maryland during the COVID-19 response to address concerns over mask mandates and school closures. The group's focus shifted to critical race theory and gender fluidity, with parents objecting to teaching that certain groups are "oppressors" or "oppressed". M4L members also expressed concern over books in elementary school libraries with explicit content and dismal proficiency scores in math and English.

title: Leave our children alone
content: Talbot County Public Schools in Easton, MD are being targeted by Moms for Liberty, an extremist organization that advocates against rights and equality. The Southern Poverty Law Center has designated Moms for Liberty as an extremist group. Candidates endorsed by Moms for Liberty in Talbot County include Anne O'Conner, Kerry Gunshenan, and Karla Wieland Cherry.

title: St. Mary's College of Maryland freezes tuition again; President announces retirement
content: St. Mary's College of Maryland froze tuition for the fifth consecutive year; President Tuajuanda Jordan announced her retirement in June 2025. The college approved a 3.9% increase in room and board rates for the 2024-25 school year due to inflation and the increased Maryland minimum wage. Outgoing Chair Susan L. Dyer led the final meeting, which also saw the election of John Bell as the new chair and approval of various board meetings and events.

title: Will Maryland’s Blueprint for education work?
content: Maryland plans to spend $16.6 billion by 2029 on its Blueprint for education, a law passed in 2021 aiming to boost student performance and quality throughout the state's schools. The Accountability and Implementation Board oversees funding and initiative implementation, monitoring progress through 92 data measures. School districts face challenges due to short planning time, limited resources, and slow communication with employees. The board can withhold funding from failing school systems and will evaluate the Blueprint's success by October.

title: Community BBQ hosted to show support for DCPS middle schooler
content: A community BBQ was hosted in Cambridge, MD, on May 8, 2024, to support sixth grader Tori Gibbs, who is Muslim and was bullied at school. The event was organized by mosques in Baltimore and Philadelphia, with organizers seeking education and change after circulating videos of the incident. Tori's mother, LaToya Gibbs, met with Dorchester County Public Schools Interim Superintendent Jymil Thompson on May 8 to discuss bullying awareness. Rian Johnson, a parent involved in the incident, has been charged with conspiracy-related crimes. The community barbecue resulted in five attendees taking their Shahada and expressing support for Tori.

title: Sandy Hill Elementary teacher dies in Hebron crash
content: Elizabeth "Lizzi" Cockey, a 23-year-old Sandy Hill Elementary teacher, was killed in a car crash on May 15, 2024, while traveling to work on U.S. Route 50 near Hebron, Maryland. She taught special education for kindergarteners and first graders at Sandy Hill Elementary School. Principal Deborah Gibson notified families of Cockey's students via a letter and spoke with each family individually. Education psychologists, social workers, and counselors provided extra support to the school community in the days following her death.

title: School superintendent proposes FY25 budget
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Dr. Karen Couch, Superintendent of Schools, proposed a FY25 budget totaling $32,175,451 for Maryland's school system. The budget includes an 85%-88% allocation to salaries and requires an additional $246,969 in county funding. Koch said she will need the county to provide nearly $1 million more than required, with the current budget balance insufficient to cover all expenses.

title: LWVQAC hosts dinner discussion on advancement of AI during election season
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Queen Anne's County League of Women Voters hosted a dinner discussion on the advancement of AI and its effects on democracy with guest speaker John Lewis, headmaster of Gunston School in Centreville, on May 7. Lewis presented an overview of AI, including machine learning, neural networks, and natural language processing, and warned of the dangers of disinformation in today's world. He advocated for information literacy, civic learning, and personal virtue as crucial pillars for a functioning democracy. The League of Women Voters emphasized the importance of voting and informed participation in government, with 60 members active in community voter services.

title: Dorchester BOE passes emergency virtual education plan with amendment
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Dorchester County Board of Education passed an emergency virtual education plan with amendments on May 22, 2024. The original plan, required by Maryland Senate bill, includes information on staffing and student instruction during prolonged emergencies. The board voted to amend the plan to make content supervisor involvement optional rather than mandatory in Schoology classrooms. The board also discussed camera usage in virtual classrooms, with concerns about bandwidth issues, and considered adding a provision for cameras to be turned off in such cases.

title: Caroline County Public Library celebrates renovation
content: Caroline County Public Library celebrated the completion of a years-long renovation on May 22, 2024. The renovated space offers various programming for patrons of different ages, including gaming stations and study rooms. Connie Kumor, an architect, led the design process, aiming to create a more friendly and open environment. Executive Director Debbie Bennett, retiring at the end of June, cited major legacies, including the Maryland State Library Capital Grant and community donations. The library was supported by state legislators and the Friends of the Library, which raised $78,000 for furniture.

title: BOE approves Sysco food services
content:
Queen Anne's County Public Schools Board of Education approved Sysco Eastern Maryland, LLC for food delivery services during its workshop meeting on May 15, 2024.
The district will join a partnership with Maryland's Shore Educational Food Service Consortium and shift to self-operational food services, saving money on management costs.
Caroline County put forth a bid for food and related items, but Sysco was the only bidder.
Sysco's contract with the district includes a clause for Queen Anne's to partner and utilize the services, with an estimated total cost of $800,000 for FY25.
The school board also approved a piggybacking contract with Cloverland Dairy, which will provide milk at a lower price.

title: Student seeks to share Choptank River history
content: Kennedy Thomason, a 2019 graduate of Ridgely's North Caroline High School, worked towards an associate's degree in liberal arts at Chesapeake College and later transferred to Washington College to major in American studies. She currently works as a digital archiving intern at the Starr Center for the American Experience, where she scans and archives content related to local African American families. Thomason plans to revamp her family's river cruise business, River City Cruise Company, to incorporate more historical tours of the Choptank River.

title: Nearly 300 Chesapeake College students celebrate graduation
content: Nearly 300 Chesapeake College students graduated on May 23, 2024. Clifford Coppersmith, president of Chesapeake College, congratulated graduates for persevering through the COVID-19 pandemic. Rob Thompson received the 2024-2026 Bounds Distinguished Teaching Chair Award, honoring Victoria Woodhull's dedication to women's rights. Zulema Delacruz Martinez was awarded the John T. Harrison Award for her academic performance and leadership in supporting Hispanic and Latino students at Chesapeake College.

title: Graduation ceremonies held for local homeschool students
content: Students from Shore Christian Fellowship in Queenstown, MD, were awarded diplomas on May 18, 2024. The Class of 2024 consists of 10 graduates, including Cody Blunt, Ashlyn Boyles, Alyssa Jastram, and others. Homeschool commencement programs have been held at the church for over a decade; this year's ceremony was attended by Pastor Tom Chandler, who congratulated the graduates' parents on their commitment to education.

title: Maryland stories: College hosts Memorial Day ceremony and flag planting
content: Cecil College hosted a Memorial Day Commemoration Ceremony on May 20-21, honoring those who died in war and military service. The ceremony featured a "Static Flag Display" with flags of different branches surrounding the American flag. Local veterans planted flags in memory of a veteran special to them. Students Gavin Roger and Ashley Kifer won a contest asking what Memorial Day means to them with an essay and drawing, respectively.

title: Easton Middle teams win Stock Market Game championships
content: Easton Middle School teams won state and regional Stock Market Game championships in the fall and spring, led by social studies teacher Edward Keeler. The winning teams were comprised of students Jordan Langrell, Cameron Rodrigue (spring), Wilmer Rodriguez Argueta, Javir Harrington, Gibson Taylor (fall), Caiden Sackett, Braden Streaker, Miles Fink (state).

title: Thank you for your service
content: Michael Feehley and Tom Carlson, two veterans, put up dozens of flags at the Easton Elks Lodge on May 26, 2024. Feehley teaches schools about the sacrifices made by veterans since the Korean War, imparting the message "All gave some and some gave all." He also tells students that veterans' families often went without during their service, reminding them not to take liberties for granted. Feehley's program aims to promote gratitude towards veterans through a teach-in at schools, with decorated veteran Tom Carlson helping to hoist flags.

title: Embrace uncertainty, Joe Flacco tells University of Delaware graduates
content: Joe Flacco addressed the University of Delaware graduates on May 29, 2024, telling them to embrace uncertainty and lean on family and friends for support as they face challenges. He shared his own experiences with self-doubt and failure in football, saying he learned to accept failure as long as he learned from it. The quarterback, who set multiple school records at UD, urged graduates to find peace by embracing uncertainty and work hard to prepare for whatever comes next.

title: 'It’s very fulfilling': Local students recognized for accomplishments
content: Kent Island High School Senior Night 2024 recognized over 100 individual students attending college, scholarship awardees, and highest performing students in each department on May 22. Principal Daniel Harding praised the Class of 2024, citing a record number of scholarship amounts received. Shelby Faery accumulated 60 credits and achieved an Associate's Degree before graduating, while being accepted into the University of Maryland College Park for fall semester. Queen Anne's County High School also recognized dual enrollment students and scholarship winners on May 16.

title: Sending Shelly home
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Shelly, a diamondback terrapin, was part of the Terrapin Program through Maryland Environmental Service and spent her first year growing at Kent County Middle School in Chestertown.
In May 2024, Shelly rode on a school bus to Tilghman Island in Talbot County and then back to Poplar Island, where she was released into the wild after being part of a research program.
The researchers aim to determine if human involvement in terrapins' early stages gives them a better chance of survival in the nature world, as part of the Paul S. Sarbanes Ecosystem Restoration Project.
Shelly's release marked an opportunity for middle school students to learn about terrapin ecology and the environmental impacts on the Chesapeake Bay.
Poplar Island was previously eroded by the Chesapeake waters, but it is now under construction with various species of wildlife calling it home.

title: Raising the future at the Talbot County Free Library
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Talbot County Free Library hosts its ninth annual Chesapeake Children's Book Festival on June 22, featuring 22 children's book authors and illustrators. The festival will include a free book voucher for participating kids, performances by the Maryland State Opera Bears, crafts, and other activities. This year marks the first time the opera bears are performing at the event. The library aims to create a fun day of learning and exploration for children.

title: Veteran Affairs Committee honors students for USO posters
content: The Veterans Affairs Committee honored students from Saints Peter and Paul High School in Easton, MD, for designing USO posters as part of a fundraiser on December 7, 2023. The committee chairman, Michael Freely, presented certificates to the students and donated to their art class. The posters were created under the guidance of art teacher Jacqui Gosselin.

title: St. Michaels High School class of 2024 advised to 'just keep swimming'
content: The St. Michaels High School Class of 2024 received their diplomas on June 2, 2024, with Senior Class President Madi White welcoming guests and congratulating her classmates. Lexi Rockwell presented the mantel to valedictorian Nathan Henckel, who quoted Hannah Montana in his speech. Talbot County Public Schools Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi advised graduates to "just keep swimming" as they move forward, having endured hardships during their four years of education.

title: 287 Easton High students get diplomas
content: 287 Easton High students received diplomas on June 2, 2024, with Principal Sherry Spurry praising their resilience. Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi focused on encouraging graduates to "be great and make mistakes." Valedictorian Iven Chen emphasized the importance of pursuing one's own path in life.

title: Class of 2024 NDHS eagles fly the nest
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

North Dorchester High School's Class of 2024 graduated on May 29, with Ta'Tyana Maradiaga and Fatima Kaleem delivering speeches about their class's experiences and future aspirations. The ceremony was held indoors due to rain, but included a memorable moment when caps flew through the auditorium stage. Valedictorian Fatima Kaleem plans to attend New York University, while Salutatorian Ta'Tyana Maradiaga will attend the University of Maryland, College Park. Principal David Stofa emphasized the importance of embracing diversity, empathy, and kindness as graduates pursue their dreams.

title: 'Unparalleled resilience, adaptability and determination:' CSD class of 2024 graduates
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Wil and Luke Reinbold, identical twin brothers, were co-valedictorians of Cambridge-South Dorchester High School's class of 2024. The class received $2.8 million in scholarships. The commencement ceremony honored the students' resilience, adaptability, and determination despite the COVID-19 pandemic. The ceremony featured speeches from Wil, Luke, CSD Principal Jerome Stover, teacher Shawn Tucker, and performances by staff and administration members.

title: Class of 2024 displays '24-karat shine'
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

June 4, 2024: The Kent County High School Class of 2024 celebrated their graduation at Trojan Stadium with Principal Kris Hemstetter leading the ceremony.
The class has many accomplishments, including dual-completer status, AP classes and exams, and dual enrollment credits.
Valedictorian Ben Loller will attend Brown University to study computer science, while salutatorian Madison Messick earned a full ride to the University of Maryland.
The Class of 2024 consists of students heading to colleges or trade schools (70%), entering the workforce (26%), enlisting in the military (4%), and others.

title: Caroline County high schools mark graduations
content: Two Caroline County high schools celebrated graduations: Colonel Richardson High School on June 5 and North Caroline High School on May 29. The graduates wore their school colors and mortar boards as they walked to the strains of "Pomp and Circumstance." Principals Jared Sherman (CRHS) and Matt Spiker (NCHS) congratulated the graduates, with Sherman praising the efforts of many people involved in the graduation.

title: Dorchester County talks Blueprint with MACo
content:
Dorchester County Council met with MACo President Johnny Olszewski and Executive Director Michael Sanderson on June 4 to discuss Blueprint for Maryland's Future requirements.
The plan, passed in 2021, aims to improve student outcomes by increasing education funding by $3.8 billion over a decade.
Maryland Association of Counties President Olszewski noted that counties beyond large ones are also feeling the pinch from the requirement.
MACo is requesting more comprehensive cost analysis and increased state aid for pre-K facility renovations as part of Blueprint implementation.
The association warns that property tax increases may be necessary due to limited space in critical areas.

title: Summer aviation, model rocket events at Easton Airport
content: The Easton Airport's Aviation Career Education Program and the Civil Air Patrol will host events for kids and teens ages 12-16 this summer, including model rocket construction and launch sessions at Easton Airport's ACE Hangar in Easton, MD, on July 23 and 24, with specific times TBD.

title: Young runners recognized by Board of Education
content: The Caroline County Board of Education recognized young runners from Greensboro Elementary for their achievements, including two running clubs that ran a 5k in Cambridge on May 4, raising $4,287 for Parkinson's awareness.

title: Done for the children
content: Barbara Lee Jefferson's therapy dogs, all female rottweilers, were approved for Alliance of Therapy Dogs and Crisis Response Canines in 2012. She has over 1,000 visits under her belt, earning National Recognition for their therapy work. In August, she was told by a teacher that dogs were no longer allowed at Easton Elementary School due to a "policy change", but the decision came without update or explanation.

title: QACPS approves piggybacking bread and paper product contracts
content: Queens Anne's County Public Schools approved piggybacking contracts with Schmidt Baking Company for bread products and FPC Distribution for cafeteria paper products, effective June 5, 2024. The fiscal impact is expected to be $140,000 for bread products and $142,000 for paper products, both from the food service fund balance.

title: High school teacher guilty of assault on prankster
content: Dylan M. Aiman, a 54-year-old teacher at Rising Sun High School, pleaded guilty to second-degree assault and received a suspended six-month sentence and 15 months of supervised probation on June 11, 2024. The incident occurred on May 4, when Aiman chased two 13-year-old boys across the street after they pranked him with a "ding dong ditch" prank at his residence in Rising Sun, Maryland.

title: Classmate's legacy lives on in Kent Island
content: Darcy Lynn, Kent Island High school's Class of 2024 valedictorian, spoke at the graduation ceremony on May 30, 2024. She honored classmate Jacob Sloan, who died in their seventh-grade year, and encouraged her peers to carry on his legacy of kindness by making the world a better place through everyday actions. Lynn also quoted Taylor Swift's advice to "be good to people" as she congratulated her classmates and urged them to embrace their future with kindness and community spirit.

title: It's official: Thompson to lead Dochester schools
content: Jymil Thompson has been selected as the next Dorchester County Public Schools superintendent after conducting a national search. He holds degrees from Pennsylvania State University, Trinity University, Howard University, and Indiana Wesleyan University. Thompson will take over the role on July 1, succeeding interim Superintendent David Bromwell, who stepped down in March. The board president praised Thompson as the "best fit" for the position.

title: Caroline Board of Education recognizes student representatives
content: Caroline County Board of Education recognized Vanessa Odidika and Kadeen Belle as Student Board Representatives for the 2024-2025 school year. Odidika is a senior at Colonel Richardson High School and plans to be a pediatric emergency physician after graduation. Belle is a junior at North Caroline High School and plans to study law after graduation. Simmons, superintendent of schools for Caroline County, described both students as outstanding representatives and welcomed their input on future decisions. The student representatives will begin their responsibilities in September.

title: DCPS approves fiscal year 2025 budget in 3 to 1 vote
content: DCPS approved fiscal year 2025 budget with a 3-1 vote on June 3, despite concerns raised by some board members and community residents. The $88.5 million operating budget includes a $7.4 million increase from the previous year, primarily due to state revenue sources. Dorchester County Public Schools Interim Superintendent Jymil Thompson made changes to the budget, including redistributing media specialists to other positions in the school system. Board member Chris Wheedleton expressed concerns about the lack of community feedback and process, while others defended the decision, citing financial constraints and the need for cost savings.

title: Rock Hall Garden Club offers yearly scholarship
content: The Rock Hall Garden Club awards a $1,000 scholarship to a high school senior each year to promote agriculture, horticulture, or natural resources. The award was given to Bradley Trice Moore II on May 16, and the club's next event is a potluck and flower show in July.

title: It's official: Thompson to lead Dochester schools
content: Jymil Thompson has been selected as the next Dorchester County Public Schools superintendent after a national search. Thompson previously served as interim superintendent since March 2 and holds degrees from Pennsylvania State University, Trinity University, Howard University, and Indiana Wesleyan University. His official start date is July 1, and he aims to improve the district's ranking and climate within schools.

title: Talbot school board passes special education staffing plan
content: The Talbot County Board of Education unanimously approved a special education staffing plan, with projected decreases in elementary students across all five schools. The plan includes maintaining current staffing levels and seven speech therapists, but board members questioned whether hours of need rather than number of students should be used to analyze staffing needs. Additional recommendations include adding a special education supervisor and four instructional assistants. Enrollment numbers are steady, with no schools overutilized, although housing development and demographic shifts may impact facilities in the future.

title: Dorchester school board Vice President Susan Morgan resigns
content: Susan Morgan, Dorchester County Board of Education vice president and former president, has resigned following a contentious vote on an alternative education program at the June 13 meeting. Morgan was the sole vote in favor of keeping Vision Quest, which would have cost the district over $3.3 million. She cited seven students who graduated this year due to the program as a reason for her support. Morgan also withdrew from running for reelection and criticized appointed board members Chris Wheedleton and Tabilah Chikwendu's approach to the board.

title: Dorchester BOE votes to terminate alternative education contract
content: The Dorchester County Board of Education voted to terminate its three-year contract with Vision Quest, an alternative education program for district high schoolers, following a tense discussion on June 13, 2024. The contract would have cost over $3.3 million and provided in-school and off-campus services for up to 10 students at any given time. Board members Chris Wheedleton, Talibah Chikwendu, and Sheri Hubbard voted in favor of termination, while Susan Morgan abstained and Mike Diaz stayed silent due to his wife's employment at Vision Quest.

title: This Juneteenth, let's prioritize education policy
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Frederick Douglass's legacy emphasizes education as a tool for liberation and equality. On Juneteenth, the US will commemorate the end of slavery, and Douglass's impact on education policy is highlighted. Prince George's County in Maryland ranks last in statewide education rankings, with high schools underperforming state targets. County Executive Angela Alsobrooks has expressed a lack of concern for the issue, opposing charter schools and school choice. Scholars suggest that these policies can positively affect student achievement, particularly for African Americans and underserved communities.

title: Mountaire Farms provides scholarships for 32 students
content: Mountaire Farms provided $2,500 scholarships to 32 students, primarily children and grandchildren of employees, growers, and grain producers. The recipients include Kiersten Anderson from Millsboro, Delaware, who will attend Delaware Technical and Community College to study nursing; Autumn Drew from Bishopville, Maryland, attending Wor-Wic Community College for environmental studies; Taylor Harding from Grasonville, Maryland, planning to attend Eastern University for nursing; and Eunsol Park, a recent immigrant from South Korea, planning to attend Wor-Wic Community College for STEM classes.

title: Mothers of Baltimore: Local women try to overcome lack of child care
content: Bridget Lang reports that in Baltimore, many neighborhood-based child care centers cater to single mothers and prioritize empathy and flexibility. Yvonne Turner's Old Mother Hubbard's Child Care Center and LaKesha Solomon's Solomon's Family Daycare offer one-on-one time with children and support the community. According to Census data, there was a 15.6% loss of registered child care providers in Baltimore City since the COVID-19 pandemic, and some centers now rely on vouchers from the Child Care Scholarship Program. Latoya Turpin's Little Steps Childcare prioritizes curriculum and development, while also keeping parents informed through an app called Brightwheel.

title: Summer Speaker Series panel empowers audience to find passion and purpose
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Women to Watch Summer Speaker Series panel empowers audience to find passion and purpose with four panelists: Shelly Gross-Wade, Kim Montooth, Shawna D. Payne, and Liz Verhelle, discussing topics such as career changes, burnout, and finding one's driving purpose. The series kicked off at Chesapeake College on June 21, 2024, and will continue with events at Wharves at Choptank Visitor Center and Avalon Theatre in July and August.

title: Maritime Museum celebrates Education Professionals
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum hosted its second annual Education Professionals Gratitude Day, celebrating educators and providing free admission to the museum for themselves and their families. The event was inspired by the hard work and dedication of educators during the COVID-19 pandemic. Jill Ferris, vice president of education and interpretation, led the initiative, which included activities such as a musical performance, shaved ice, and Harbor Highlights cruises. Educators from nationwide attended, including Mia Alvarez and Michelle McDaniel, who praised the museum's interactive exhibits and hands-on learning experiences. The event aims to recognize and support educators' efforts in educating the next generation.

title: Schools should do better
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 3-5 concise sentences:

Jymil Thompson, new school superintendent of Dorchester County, discussed increasing the district's ranking from 23rd to improve its performance. The counties on Maryland's Eastern Shore have varying school district ratings: Worcester County ranks 3rd, Queen Anne's County ranks 8th, and Dorchester County ranks 22nd. A comparison of two websites found slight discrepancies in rankings among these counties.

title: Wearing hoods, having cellphones on are not allowed in Calvert schools
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Calvert County Public Schools will ban students from wearing hoods in school buildings starting August. The decision was made after a survey showed majority support for the ban, citing difficulties in identifying students with hidden earbuds. The policy change also affects cellphone usage, requiring devices to be powered off and kept secure during school hours.

title: FOR THE RECORD
content: Chrissy Bartz's swearing-in as Caroline County Board of Education member was postponed from June 18 to an unspecified date. A story previously published by The Times Record incorrectly stated she had been sworn in on June 18.

title: Caroline Commissioners approve CCPS FY25 budget summary
content: Caroline County Public Schools Superintendent Derek Simmons presented a $94.48 million balanced operating budget for fiscal year 2025, an increase of nearly $4 million from the previous year. The district feels financially stable despite rising expenditures and cost-of-business increases, including new positions funded by expiring COVID-19 grants. Commissioners approved the budget summary, with Vice President Larry Porter asking about progress toward reaching a $60,000 starting teacher salary mandate by 2026.

title: County approves budget transfers for Talbot schools
content: Talbot County Public Schools requested approval from the county council to make categorical transfers in its FY24 budget, including $75,000 for student services and $500,000 for transportation. The district also sought $600,000 for fixed charges related to other postemployment benefits contributions and health insurance prepayments. Savings from instructional salaries ($850,000) were used to transfer funds. Council members expressed concerns about filling vacant positions but ultimately approved the request unanimously on June 27, 2024.

title: KCHS valedictorian codes bus program for families
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

Ben Loller, Kent County High School's Class of 2024 valedictorian and Brown University-bound student, created a coding project to track students' school buses using web-based software and location transmission hardware.
Loller served on the Board of Education's Citizen Advisory Committee and raised the idea for such a program after discussing it with other parents and committee members.
The project was developed in collaboration with William Poore, Kent County Public Schools' supervisor of information technology, as part of the Makerspace program.
