Loller presented his work to the Kent County Board of Education on May 28, 2024, and received praise from board members and school administrators.
Loller plans to continue working on the project at Brown University in Rhode Island this fall.

title: Diaz resigns from Dorchester Board of Education
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Mike Diaz resigned as president of the Dorchester County Board of Education on June 28 due to health and family concerns, effective July 1. He underwent a liver transplant in February and nearly died from an infection in May before resigning. Diaz's resignation follows that of Vice President Susan Morgan's mid-June departure amidst conflicts within the board. The board will hold a special meeting next week for an election, with Diaz initially planning to run for reelection but unsure if he will withdraw.

title: Finding childcare in Maryland is hard. Finding good childcare is even harder
content:
Stephanie Jovine searched for child care in 2015 and found two bad options; she finally found a suitable program at LiLi's Child Care Center in Temple Hills after six months of searching.
Maryland offers a rating system to help parents select child care facilities, but providers say it is difficult to navigate.
Many families struggle with the state's scholarship program, which can have long wait times and complex requirements.
Jovine discovered the program too late for her first child, Lily, born in February 2023, and initially had to pay out of pocket; she later received temporary aid through the program's fast-track option.
A new fast-track program aims to reduce wait times, but providers complain about delays in receiving scholarship payments.

title: La Plata siblings commemorate D-Day in Normandy
content: Jack Compton, a rising sophomore at La Plata High School, and Lauren Compton, a rising senior, attended the 80th anniversary of D-Day in Normandy, France, representing their Civil Air Patrol squadron. They raised over $8,000 to make the trip possible and participated in memorial ceremonies, including one at Brittany American Cemetery and Memorial, where they stood at attention for an hour-long ceremony. The siblings visited the La Cambe German Military Cemetery and met author Chris Langlois, who wrote a book about Easy Company, a unit that included Lauren's relative Lynn "Buck" Compton.

title: Young author presents local bird guide to Horizons students
content: Xaviana Leis presented her self-published "Maryland Bird Guide" to Horizons of Kent and Queen Anne's students at the Gunston School on June 25, 2024. The book focuses on local birds common to Maryland and nearby states, with over fifty species illustrated in vibrant watercolor. Xaviana, a 13-year-old homeschool student from Edgewater, is a Girl Scout and raptor volunteer who aims to educate her community about wildlife conservation. Her goal is to continually promote environmental awareness through her book and other projects, including raising over $10,000 for Owl Moon Raptor Center.

title: Dorchester County Council president, VP thank Board of Education leadership after resignations
content: Dorchester County Council President Lenny Pfeffer and Vice President Mike Detmer thanked Dorchester County Board of Education members Mike Diaz and Susan Morgan for their service on July 2, following their resignations. Diaz resigned June 28 due to family and health concerns after undergoing a liver transplant in February. Morgan resigned June 14 amid controversy over terminating the Vision Quest contract, citing dissatisfaction with the Council's direction.

title: Local district hikes school lunch, milk prices
content: Queen Anne's County Public Schools approved a 15-cent per meal price increase and 5-cent per milk carton price increase for the 2024-2025 school year on June 26, citing cost increases. The price increases are based on the Maryland Department of Education Paid Lunch Equity Tool and minimum wage increases to $15 an hour. Meal prices will be as follows: breakfast $1.75, elementary lunch $2.75, middle school/high school lunch $3, staff lunch $4.25, and milk cartons 55 cents each.

title: 'It didn't die with her:' New Beginnings continues to grow after death of executive director
content: Theresa Stafford, executive director of New Beginnings Youth and Family Services from 2016 to 2024, died in December after battling cancer. The learning center on Greenwood Avenue continues to grow with donations, including a $25,000 gift from friend Phil Feldman to name the center after Stafford. Plans are underway to rename the center "Dr. Theresa Stafford's New Beginnings Learning Academy" and hold a dedication event later this summer. New Beginnings recently received grant awards, including a $10,000 grant from the John and Janice Wyatt Foundation for reading programming.

title: Dorchester County Council makes appointments to vacant Board of Education seats
content: Dorchester County Council appointed Brandy Dawson Cumberland and Christine LaMonica to fill Board of Education vacancies created by Mike Diaz's and Susan Morgan's resignations. Cumberland was appointed to District 1, while LaMonica was appointed to District 3. The appointments took effect immediately. Cumberland and LaMonica will prioritize a "safe learning environment," school safety, transparency, academic excellence, and support for educators.

title: Commissioners keep Master Gardeners rooted in the Kent
content: Kent County Commissioners awarded approximately $20,000 to keep the Master Gardeners program running, including funding for a part-time Master Gardener Coordinator and Horticulture Educator. The program, established in 2007, provides free educational programming and services valued at $29,369 in 2023. Kent County Master Gardeners had visited commissioners due to concerns about disbanding the program. President Ron Fithian, Albert Nickerson, and John Price unanimously voted in favor of the funding request.

title: Stronger defense, improved education
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

National defense and youth education are being overlooked by politicians, despite being long-term concerns. The latest national defense budget proposes reduced military readiness spending, while interest payments on federal debt may soon surpass defense spending. Meanwhile, increased public funding for education has not led to improving academic outcomes, threatening global competitiveness and domestic innovation.

title: Girl Scouts build gaga ball pit at Ridgely park
content: Girl Scouts from Troop 896 and Troop 899 built a Gaga Ball Pit at Martin Sutton Park in Ridgely, MD. The project was completed on June 2, 2024, after nine months of planning and advocacy for a community need. The girls worked with their dads to construct the pit, learning basic construction skills along the way. This Bronze Award service project aimed to create a fun and inclusive space for families and children in Ridgely and surrounding communities.

title: Dorchester BOE elects board leadership, approves alternative education contract
content: The Dorchester County Board of Education unanimously elected Sheri Hubbard as president and Talibah Chikwendu as vice president on July 18, 2024. Brandy Dawson Cumberland and Christine LaMonica were sworn in as District 1 and District 3 board members, respectively. The board approved a one-year contract with Transforming Lives for an alternative education program for elementary and middle school students, costing $950,000. Jymil Thompson, DCPS Superintendent, announced the district plans to replace "alternative education" with a new term.

title: 2 new Dorchester Board of Education members sworn in
content: Brandy Dawson Cumberland and Christine LaMonica were sworn in as new members of the Dorchester Board of Education on July 18, 2024. They were appointed by the Dorchester County Council to fill District 1 and District 3 seats after resignations from former board President Mike Diaz and Vice President Susan Morgan. The new board members join President Sherri Hubbard, Vice President Talibah Chikwendu, and Chris Wheedleton, with DCPS Superintendent Jymil Thompson welcoming Cumberland and LaMonica to improve the district's ranking in Maryland.

title: Rotary Club of Cambridge visits Ruark Boat Works
content: The Rotary Club of Cambridge visited the Richardson Maritime Museum and Ruark Boat Works on July 23, 2024. Rotarian Dave Williams gave the guests a tour of the facilities, explaining their Educational Program, which teaches young people about woodworking and tool use. The club also toured the boat building facility, where they saw how projects are constructed to provide added strength.

title: Men For Change recognizes volunteers' service
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Men For Change recognized six individuals, including Brandy James, Stephanie Brohawn, William Eric Smith, Cynthia Fletcher, Cederick Turner, and Roberta Butler, for their work in mentoring youth and community service. The event was held on July 20 at the Federalsburg Volunteer Fire Company banquet hall and featured keynote speaker Vaughn Evans Sr. The organization's theme this year was "Let's Get Busy" and aims to support young people with resources to become successful leaders. Men For Change is partnering with the Federalsburg Activity Center for an after-school mentoring program, which is expected to open by September.

title: Talbot County pledges support for Chesapeake College project
content: Talbot County Council approved a letter of intent to fund a $56 million Chesapeake College facility project with an estimated cost of $3 million for the county. The project will support trade programs including agricultural, electrical, and HVAC. Chesapeake College representatives expressed support for the project which will benefit counties served by the college, including Talbot County, Caroline County, Dorchester County, Queen Anne's County, and Kent County.

title: Talbot Mentors calling for more volunteers
content: Talbot Mentors has seen a 34% decrease in mentor volunteers since the pandemic, with volunteer numbers currently ranging from 50-60 mentors. Kentavius Jones, executive director of Talbot Mentors, is seeking "meaningful connections" and has piloted a peer-to-peer program pairing high schoolers with elementary school students. The organization also offers the Scholars program, which provides tutoring, college admissions assistance, and scholarship research to first-generation and marginalized students. Joan Evans, a mentor for over six years, encourages others to volunteer, stating that being a mentor requires no particular skill beyond providing time and attention.

title: ‘Stretched very thin’: Child care providers in Talbot County seeing long waitlists
content: Critchlow Adkins Children's Centers in Talbot County has over 100 children on its waitlist for preschool and before- and after-school care services, with some families waiting under a year old. The nonprofit plans to expand its facility at Chapel District Elementary School, doubling capacity from 30 to 60 children, by next year. Barbra Diaz, director of the Talbot County Center for Children and Families, notes that staffing is the main challenge in the program's Early Head Start initiative. The Lab Child Care Center in Easton also has a rolling waitlist for under-2-year-olds due to rising costs and state scholarship program issues.

title: QACPS celebrates record-breaking success in scholastic art & writing awards
content: Queen Anne's County Public Schools achieved a record-breaking success in the 2024 Scholastic Art & Writing Awards with students from Kent Island High School and Queen Anne's County High School earning honors. The district had 139 entries, winning 24 Gold Keys, 17 Silver Keys, and 47 Honorable Mentions. National Medalists Jackson Powell (Kent Island) and Casey Johnson (Queen Anne's County) received recognition for their exceptional talent.

title: Maryland READS presents to State Board of Education
content: Maryland READS presented updates and a drafted literacy policy to the Maryland State Department of Education on July 23, 2024. Founded in 2021 by Executive Director Trish Brennan-Gac, the organization aims to improve reading instruction using research data and evidence-based practices. Maryland READS focuses on three systems of support: improving instruction, building thriving reading ecosystems, and addressing barriers to reading proficiency. The group has recently wrapped up its summer series convenings and will compile meeting data for implementing feedback and continuous improvement.

title: Chrome City fundraiser revs up Benedictine's Ridgely campus
content: Benedictine School held its 22nd annual Chrome City Fundraiser on July 27, 2024, at its Ridgely campus. The event drew hundreds of car and motorcycle enthusiasts, with proceeds supporting the school's mission to care for individuals with developmental disabilities and autism. The event featured live music, food trucks, and a car and motorcycle show, with over $100,000 raised last year. Key sponsors included PRS Guitars, Queenstown Bank, and others.

title: Carefully vet candidates
content: Moms For Liberty co-founder Bridget Zielgler was involved in an investigation, and the organization's mission statement is to defend parents' rights at all levels of government. The group has members running for positions affecting school children in Talbot County, which raises concerns about infiltrating the school system with their doctrine. The MFL manifesto does not mention the rights of children. The author, Sharon Harrington, plans to carefully vet candidates who are part of the organization.

title: Reading League presents to state board
content: The Reading League of Maryland presented to the Maryland State Board of Education on July 23. The organization, a nonprofit chapter of the National Reading League, aims to advance evidence-based literacy instruction and practices. Founded in 2021, it provides professional learning opportunities for teachers, administrators, and parents, aligned with the Science of Reading.

title: Maryland Corps, Service Year Option graduates reflect on their experiences
content: In July 2024, around 235 people graduated from the Maryland Corps and Service Year Option programs in their first class. The state-run programs allowed participants to gain experience, crucial contacts, and learn about giving back to their communities. Graduates such as Brad Krantz of St. Michaels secured jobs at Talisman Therapeutic Riding up to $15/hour, while Emma Bush of Salisbury built skills for her future career through time management, resume building, and financial trainings. The programs were launched by the state last year in partnership with Historically Black Colleges and Universities and community colleges.

title: MSDE presents draft literacy policy
content: The Maryland State Department of Education presented a draft literacy policy to stakeholders on July 23, led by Deputy State Superintendent Deann Collins and Executive Director Tenette Smith. The proposed policy aims to address achievement gaps in literacy, particularly among students from minority groups living in poverty. Research suggests that early reading proficiency is critical for long-term academic success and future opportunities. The comprehensive policy draft includes four components: teacher support, assessment and parent notification, instruction and intervention, and retention and intervention.

title: St. Mary's board announces new school cellphone infractions
content: St. Mary's public schools' superintendent Scott Smith has instituted a new cellphone policy starting July 17. The policy restricts phone use to lunch hour for high school students and prohibits middle school and elementary school students from using their devices during the school day. Consequences include confiscation of phones, parental notification, and disciplinary codes, with repeat offenders facing more severe penalties.

title: Strawberry named to Talbot Board of Education
content: Dyshekia Strawberry was appointed by Gov. Wes Moore to fill a vacancy on Talbot County's Board of Education. She resides in Easton and has two children in the school district. Strawberry was sworn in during the board's meeting at the Talbot County Education Center. She was chosen to replace Jymil Thompson, who resigned from his District 1 seat to become interim superintendent of Dorchester County Public Schools. Strawberry will serve until a successor is elected in 2026.

title: One-way conversation on schools
content: Mary Yancey wrote a letter to the editor criticizing a one-way mailing about her county schools in Easton, MD on August 16, 2024, noting that 17.2% math proficiency is "well below" the state average of 25%.

title: Delaware school boards increasingly see controversy
content: Delaware school boards are experiencing increasing controversy, with tensions rising between board members and community attendees at recent meetings. The Christina School District's Board of Education has been particularly contentious, with a nearly four-and-a-half-hour meeting marked by heated comments and a state legislator filing a FOIA violation against the board. Brandywine also faced an FOIA allegation in the spring, while Capital School District's former superintendent cited a hostile work environment and interference from the board in her resignation. Advocacy groups like DelawareCAN are working to provide resources and training for school board members to improve transparency and governance, but some worry that public perception of polarized boards will make it harder to find qualified candidates.

title: Summer Youth Program Graduation at EVFC
content: Easton Volunteer Fire Department hosted a graduation program for 46 students who completed the Upper Shore Workforce Investment Board's six-week youth program on July 14, 2024. The program, designed for students with learning disabilities and handicaps, placed them in jobs across five counties including Aaron's Place, Dorchester Parks and Recreation, and Kent County Animal Shelter. Students like Connor Swann, who has since completed a veterinary assistant program at Chesapeake College, graduated with the majority retaining their jobs after completion of the course.

title: DCPS to offer new service for middle and high schoolers who can't attend in person
content: Dorchester County Public Schools will offer a new virtual synchronous instruction service for middle and high school students who require home and hospital services or cannot attend in person due to health reasons. The Edmentum agreement was approved by the board, with costs estimated at $200 per student per course, totaling around $100,000. Secondary students will receive instruction from real teachers throughout the week, while elementary students requiring services outside of school will still receive tutoring.

title: Talbot County Free Library hosts youth STEAM Camp
content: Talbot County Free Library hosted a two-week STEAM camp for elementary and middle school students in Easton, MD. The program was designed by three local high school students and funded by a grant from the Council of Friends of the Talbot County Free Library. The camp included activities such as tie-dyeing shirts, print-making tote bags, and making slime, with volunteers guiding and assisting the campers.

title: Lack of funding a 'recipe of frustration'
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 3-5 concise sentences:

Up to 200 individuals gathered at the Queen Anne's County Public Schools Board of Education building to show support for proposed layoffs of essential support staff members. The Queen Anne's County Education Association (QACEA) and local affiliates met to discuss budget transparency, citing a lack of funding as the cause of the proposed cuts. Superintendent Patricia Saelens stated that the school system is facing a $2 million deficit due to underfunding and inflation, but claims that measures such as furloughs were explored before proposing layoffs. The QACEA, along with local affiliates, plans to continue advocating for changes through dialogue and collaboration.

title: TCPS superintendent addresses mailers questioning district spending
content: Talbot County Public Schools Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi addressed mailers questioning district spending, stating there were inaccurate monetary figures and acknowledging work to be done in math education, which is a priority. The mailers, sent by Pay Attention America Inc., contained claims of low student proficiency rates and questioned the district's spending. A Board of Education work session in September will show recent state testing data, contradicting some claims made in the mailers.

title: Annual Back to School Resource Fair: Preparing students for success
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

For All Seasons hosted an annual Back to School Resource Fair at Idlewild Park on August 22, 2024. The event brought together over 25 organizations and over 1,700 people, providing hundreds of pre-stuffed backpacks with school supplies for students. Beth Anne Dorman, president of For All Seasons, emphasized the importance of community support in setting up students for success. Organizations such as Appleseed Books provided additional resources like free children's books and dental care kits. The event has grown significantly since its origin six years ago and will expand to a larger venue next year due to high demand.

title: Family holding out hope for turf field project at Easton High
content: Turf field project at Easton High School uncertain; Elgin Hawley's wish was granted with Make-A-Wish Mid-Atlantic support in July 2023. $1.5 million allocated for outstanding capital projects, including turf field, which has an estimated price of $1.8 million. Talbot County Public Schools received funding from the county and made a commitment to partner with Make-A-Wish. Elgin Hawley's aneurysm led her to wish for a turf field; she graduated this spring after returning to school in February 2022.

title: Talbot schools welcome back teachers and staff
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Talbot County Public Schools hosted an Opening Day celebration at Easton High School, welcoming new teachers and presenting staff with awards. Jeremy Hillyard was named Teacher of the Year, and Rosario Steele received the Support Staff of the Year award. District Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi spoke about major areas for focus, including staffing, transportation, and student behavior, while emphasizing three priorities: academic equity in math, an engaging environment, and recruiting a more diverse staff.

title: Courage needed by Blueprint Accountability Board
content: The Blueprint Accountability and Implementation Board is concerned about inadequate funding for Maryland's education system, with shortfalls in classroom essentials, interventions for struggling learners, and career and technology education. The governor and General Assembly have not addressed these issues despite growing evidence of the problem. The board has the power to recommend legislative changes to address the funding shortfall and can use its reports to track compliance with state requirements. Funding is crucial for implementing the Blueprint's ambitious goals, including intensive interventions in all grades.

title: Chapel District Elementary breaks ground on renovation project
content: Chapel District Elementary School broke ground on its renovation project on August 24, 2024, with a ceremony led by Talbot County Public Schools Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and Principal Kari Clow. The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company is leading the $26.9 million project, which began construction on August 5, 2024. The school was built in 1952 and last renovated in 1994. Construction is expected to take a couple years, with additional learning space, a new media center, and playground renovations included in the project.

title: Students head back to school in Talbot County
content: Students returned to Easton Elementary School on August 26, 2024, for the new school year. Principal Lisa Devaric welcomed students and staff, noting a full staff of certified positions with 189 people on campus. Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi emphasized the importance of collaboration and community, citing a focus on multilingual learners and confidence-building.

title: State test scores: Local districts increase in English and math, dip in science
content: The Maryland State Department of Education released 2023-2024 test scores showing a 0.5% statewide increase in English proficiency and a 0.8% statewide increase in math proficiency. Talbot County Public Schools increased in English (2.8%) and math (1.1%) proficiency, but fell below state averages in science with drops of 12.6% and 9.1%. Caroline County Public Schools showed increases in math (3.9%) and reading (2.1%), while Dorchester County Public Schools rose in English (1.4%) and math (1%) but dipped in science (12.1%).

title: Pastoral Ponderings: Back to school
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Pastor Kevin Wall advises parents to prepare themselves and their children for school by getting physical supplies needed for school while also spiritually preparing them. Pastor Shelby Turner suggests committing to daily prayer for areas such as safety, friendships, academic success, character growth, faith, friends, academics, character, and safety and success. Parents can use scriptures like Ephesians 3:14-19, Romans 12:2, Proverbs 2:6, Deuteronomy 31:6, Psalms 91:1, and Colossians 3:23 in their prayers.

title: Plans to address test scores, cell phones shared by district staff at Moms for Liberty meeting
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Talbot County Public Schools held a meeting with Moms for Liberty to address concerns about education, including low math scores and student cell phone use. Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi shared news of new research-based curriculums and added positions, such as math coaches, to help improve education. Attendees expressed concern over anonymous postcards criticizing the district's finances and highlighting lower-than-average math proficiency. Pepukayi introduced a program called YONDER, which uses cell phone pouches to limit usage during school hours.

title: Leonard Hall Junior Naval Academy prepares for move after a century
content: Leonard Hall Junior Naval Academy is preparing to move after a century due to its lease not being renewed by St. Mary's County commissioners in January 2024. The academy, with 15 students and six teachers, currently operates on a month-to-month lease and is exploring new locations in the county. A move could be made as early as this fall, requiring "a lot of logistics" to relocate after 115 years at its current location. Leonard Hall Board of Trustees President Amie Milan aims to increase enrollment to 100 students to achieve a stable year for the academy's students.

title: "ArtScene | the Podcast" kicks off new season, new school year
content: "ArtScene | The Podcast" launched a new episode on September 1, 2024, featuring Centreville Middle School art teacher Jackie Jablecki. Jablecki shares her journey from personal loss to professional triumph in the classroom, highlighting her passion for art and education. She discusses transformative power of TAB classrooms and student-centered approach. Jablecki is involved with the Art of Education University, where she completed her Master's degree.

title: Time to reframe conversation about literacy
content: The Maryland State Department of Education's draft literacy policy aims to establish a framework to support students and teachers by providing tools, training, and resources for teachers to foster foundational reading skills. The policy includes components such as early screening and assessment, professional learning, coaching, and a Student Reading Improvement Plan. A toolkit is being developed to communicate with parents in plain language. The focus of the conversation should shift from retention to empowering children to become fluent readers.

title: Aiming to fly: Civil Air Patrol holds open house for young, aspiring pilots
content: The Civil Air Patrol held an open house at the St. Mary's County Regional Airport on August 28 to introduce young potential members to its cadet program, which offers career exploration in aviation and military service. The program is open to members aged 12-21 and provides opportunities for flying, search and rescue, community service, and wilderness survival training. Local residents attended the event, including parents and children who expressed interest in joining the program after learning about its values and activities.

title: Dorchester students return to school
content: Students in Dorchester County returned to school on September 3-4, 2024, for the beginning of the 2024-25 school year, with first through sixth graders starting classes on Tuesday and ninth graders following the next day.

title: High School Brigade charms with '70s songs
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Kent County High School's Brigade of Blue performed "Copacabana" by Barry Manilow and "September," by Earth, Wind and Fire during their two-week band camp, led by Band Director Jodi Bortz. The marching band also held their annual "Turning Blue to Gold" ceremony honoring students who acquired musical skills. Mirelle Kraus led the color guard, looking forward to the fall events, including a homecoming football game on September 13 against Arcadia High School.

title: New student board member sworn-in
content: Alden Swanson, a rising junior at Kent County High School, was sworn-in as the newest member of the Kent County Board of Education on August 12. She will serve a one-year term and provide a monthly report, cast an advisory vote, and offer student perspective on issues. Swanson was elected by her peers at Kent County High School and is a member of the cross country team and band.

title: School lunches through the years
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

* School lunches have changed over the years but remain important for students' success.
* Marie Savage shares recipes from her childhood in the 1950s, such as bologna sandwiches and homemade soup.
* Modern school lunch ideas include BBQ Chicken Cups, PB&J Apples, Pickle Roll Ups, Turkey Club Roll Ups, Grilled Cheese Roll Ups, Nutella Banana Sushi, Ham, Mac N Cheese Muffins, Rice Krispie Peanut Butter Bananas, Pepperoni Pizza Sticks, and other creative options.

title: County agrees to audit of school system financial records
content: Queen Anne's County Commissioners unanimously approved hiring an independent auditing firm to conduct a performance audit of the Queen Anne's County Public School Board of Education's financial records and budgetary development procedures on September 10, 2024. The audit aims to assess operational decisions, evaluate the finance office, and ensure no fraud is occurring. The Board of Education faces challenges including significant turnover in its accounting function and requests for increased funding despite flat student enrollment numbers. The county allocated $75.1 million and an additional $42.1 million in state funding for FY 25, but the board has a projected budgetary deficit just six weeks into FY 25.

title: Caroline County pilots cell phone pouches in schools, other districts to follow
content: Caroline County Public Schools have implemented a policy where students put their phones in locked pouches during school hours to prevent usage. The Yondr pouches are being tested at Colonel Richardson Middle School and Lockerman Middle School, with Talbot and Dorchester counties planning to follow suit later this fall. Caroline County Superintendent Derek Simmons hopes to track improvements in student discipline and focus if the pilot yields positive results, potentially extending the policy to high schools.

title: First Friday ice cream social welcomes new Washington College students to town
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Washington College students gathered with local organizations and vendors in downtown Chestertown for an ice cream social on September 6, marking the start of the fall semester. Mayor David Foster welcomed students to town, sharing historic facts about Chestertown. President Mike Sosulski congratulated the largest incoming class ever and encouraged students to explore the college's offerings, including a growing commitment to free expression.

title: Birding and boating the Harriet Tubman Byway
content: A tour group combined birding and boating along the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Scenic Byway in Caroline and Dorchester Counties on September 14, 2024. The event featured guides Alex Green and Jim Rapp, who highlighted sites such as Linchester Mill, The Webb Cabin, and the Caroline County Courthouse. Tourists including Jeanea Blair from Baltimore learned about Harriet Tubman's life and work while spotting 25 species of birds.

title: Easton High teacher named finalist for Maryland Teacher of the Year
content: Jeremy Hillyard, a Spanish and English as a second language math teacher at Easton High School, is one of seven finalists for Maryland Teacher of the Year. He was named Talbot County Public Schools' 2024-25 Teacher of the Year in April. Hillyard will attend a reception in Baltimore on October 4 to compete for the top award.

title: Rotary club members learn about All4Love
content: Lucas Thorpe, co-founder and executive director of All4Love, spoke to Rotary Club of Cambridge members about the organization's work with youth in Dorchester County. He founded All4Love 10 years ago with Khail Johnson, a brotherly love based on their interest in youth mentoring. The organization aims to improve lives of adolescents and young adults in the Cambridge community through programs like high school mentoring, flag football, breakfast clubs, and after-school music programs.

title: For Dorchester superintendent, it's all about teaching and learning
content: Dorchester County Public Schools Superintendent Jymil Thompson visits classrooms and schools every week to create a comfortable atmosphere of teaching and learning, offering guidance when needed. Since becoming superintendent in June, Thompson aims to improve student success by focusing on instructional leadership, targeting a ranking increase from 23rd to 15th in four years. The district identified steps to achieve this goal, including coaching and professional development support for administrators, aiming to develop "great instructional leaders."

title: Talbot school board sees test scores, improvement initiatives
content: Talbot County Public Schools saw slight increases in math and English proficiency levels, with 47.3% of students proficient in English and 18.3% in math as of the 2023-2024 Maryland Comprehensive Assessment Program. The district, led by Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and Assistant Superintendent Helga Einhorn, tracks student learning levels through internal benchmarks. Talbot County ranks 14th and 18th among 24 districts in English and math proficiency, respectively. Experts will review three elementary schools in Talbot County, including White Marsh Elementary, which showed significant growth in math achievement.

title: Easton flying event gets women up in the air
content: The Maryland Chapter of the Ninety-Nines hosted the first-ever Let's Fly Now event at Easton Airport on September 14, 2024. The event gave 21 women, including Maria Esparraguera and Cheryl Mohrmann, who piloted two flights, the chance to learn about planes and sit in the passenger seat with a pilot taking flight. The event aimed to encourage more women to fly planes, with attendees ranging from local teens to a woman who drove from Brooklyn, New York. The event was well-received, with attendees showing enthusiasm for flying and interest in future events.

title: Constitution Alliance hosts Liberty and Freedom event in Easton for 3rd year
content: The Mid-Shore Constitution Alliance hosted "Our Journey to Liberty and Freedom" event on September 17 at the Academy Art Museum in Easton, MD. Renowned actors Darius Wallace (as Frederick Douglass) and Kurt Smith (as Thomas Jefferson) delivered powerful performances discussing liberty, freedom, and the U.S. Constitution. State Sen. Johnny Mautz attended the event, which also honored new US citizens and featured a color guard, town crier, and Sons of the American Revolution in period costumes.

title: St. Michaels reading specialist receives Fulbright award
content: Kelly Coutts, a reading specialist at St. Michaels Elementary School, received a Fulbright Teacher Exchange award for the 2024-2025 cycle from the U.S. Department of State and the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board on September 20, 2024. Coutts will participate in an online course and research abroad, with details of her destination to be revealed later. The award recognizes her hard work and dedication to Talbot County students, following a tradition of over 800 U.S. citizens who teach, study or conduct research abroad through the Fulbright Program each year.

title: Kaitlyn Wright named state Teacher of the Year finalist
content: Kaitlyn Wright, a Kent County Middle School teacher, is among seven finalists for Maryland Teacher of the Year. She was previously named Kent County Public Schools' Teacher of the Year last spring and will undergo an interview process in September with a panel of state judges. The next Maryland Teacher of the Year will be announced in October 2024.

title: Talbot school board discusses concerns over athletic fields
content: Talbot County Board of Education discussed athletic fields on September 20, 2024, with concerns over costs and maintenance. The district has $1.5 million for capital projects, including an estimated $1.8 million for an artificial turf field at Easton High School. Other projects include auditorium lights, a basketball court, stadium lights, and a new playground, totaling $3.36 million. Board members emphasized the need for information on field maintenance costs before committing funding.

title: Dorchester MCAP data shows some progress, some areas of concern
content: Dorchester County Public Schools' Spring 2024 MCAP scores show year-to-year increases in English and math proficiency rates. The district ranked 22nd in English and 21st in math, with notable improvements in fifth grade science and middle school algebra. Concerns remain about support pathway classes, elementary English scores, and literacy plan implementation. Superintendent Jymil Thompson noted the score increases as progress, while Assistant Superintendent Jodi Colman highlighted growth areas and called for further improvement.

title: Dorchester schools to create strategic plan for coming years
content: Dorchester County Public Schools is developing a strategic plan with Integrated Impact Group from Pennsylvania for the years 2025-2028. Consultant Connie Casson led the meeting on September 19, outlining the process and goals, including preparing students, recruiting and retaining staff, and exploring career opportunities in local industries. The district will review data and research other districts through September and October, followed by community meetings to gather ideas and priorities starting October 14 at Hurlock United Methodist Church.

title: Multicultural Resource Center awards scholarships to 14 students
content: The Chesapeake Multicultural Resource Center awarded scholarships to 14 students in September 2024, providing over $35,000 for the upcoming fall term. The scholarship was established about four years ago and is designed for first-generation college students with financial need. Winners include Morgan Lewis, who plans to pursue a master's and doctoral degree in psychology.

title: Washington College Electric Boat Team visits Radcliffe Creek School
content: The Washington College Electric Boat Team visited Radcliffe Creek School on September 20, with President Douglas Hewes and advisor Brian Palmer sharing their team's success story. The team won first place in multiple races against top engineering programs, overcoming design failures to achieve success. They broke the Guinness World Record for the greatest distance by an electric boat on a single charge without solar on September 2.

title: Child care priority needed
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maryland's average annual cost of infant care ($15,335) exceeds the state's average rent, pushing 40% of families with young children into debt. The author, Julie Leitch, a single mother in Talbot County, struggles to afford childcare until her son enters public school at age 5. 89% of voters want candidates to have a plan for affordable childcare. Leaders are urged to prioritize child care in their first 100 days if elected.

title: Two student representatives appointed to Talbot Board of Education
content: Two student representatives were appointed to the Talbot County Board of Education: Gabriella Streaker and Brynn Lizewski. They were sworn in as student board members on September 18, 2024. Streaker is a senior at Easton High School, while Lizewski is a senior at St. Michaels Middle High School.

title: Baltimore fire cuts internet in Talbot schools, libraries
content: A fire in Baltimore's manhole burned fiber optic cable in a 'Sailor Network' hub affecting Talbot County Public Schools and libraries on September 30, 2024. The outage impacted internet service for all schools, with phone service also affected at Easton Elementary School. Internet was restored to schools by 3:30 p.m. Tuesday.

title: Washington College Electric Boat Team visits Radcliffe Creek School
content: The Washington College Electric Boat Team visited Radcliffe Creek School on September 20, 2024, and shared their success story with students. The team's president, Douglas Hewes, spoke about designing strategies that led to winning first place in multiple races against top universities like Princeton University. Team members Mac Sansbury, Tiyaba Jamil, and adviser Brian Palmer discussed their approach to building better batteries, electric motors, solar technology, and hull designs.

title: Four years after her murder, Madison Sparrow's legacy lives on
content: Madison Sparrow was a 17-year-old Newark Charter School student murdered by her ex-boyfriend and friend in Delaware on October 2, 2020. Four years later, her legacy lives on through five scholarship recipients pursuing careers in education, funded by the Madison Sparrow Scholarship. Heather Sparrow Murphy, Madison's mother, continues to raise funds for the scholarship and participate in victim-offender dialog programs to help heal. Murphy forgave her daughter's murderers before sentencing and has since been involved with the nonprofit Victims' Voices Heard. The Love Wins 5K race, now in its fourth year, supports the scholarship fund and helps Murphy keep Madison's memory alive.

title: How Maryland schools are cracking down on cell phones this fall
content: Maryland schools are cracking down on cell phones this fall, with at least a third of public schools tightening up rules to keep devices off and out of sight. The new rules apply to instruction periods, even on school buses in some areas around Baltimore. Two middle schools in Caroline County have implemented a pilot program requiring students to lock their phones in pouches during the day. Supt. Derek L. Simmons in Caroline County and Supt. Scott Smith in St. Mary's County are among administrators promoting the measures.

title: Talbot Board of Education candidates speak at town hall forum
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Candidates for Talbot County Board of Education fielded questions during an open forum on October 4, 2024, discussing standardized test scores, student engagement and teacher retention. Incumbents Candace Henry, Ann O'Connor, Anna Howie, and Cynthia Jurrius attended the forum, with scores showing slight improvements in math and English proficiency rates, but all candidates agreed that test scores must improve. The District 6 seat is a race between Kerry Gunshenan and Cynthia Jurrius, while residents will see the respective school board candidates on the ballot on November 5, 2024.

title: Forum notable for absent candidates
content: Four candidates - Candace Henry, Ann O'Connor, Anna Howie, and Cynthia Jurrius - attended a Community Town Hall event in Easton, MD on October 5, 2024, where they were interviewed by moderators and audience members. The event was notable for the absence of other candidates.

title: QACPS joins insulin litigation class action lawsuit
content: The Queen Anne's County Public Schools Board of Education joined a lawsuit against companies for price gouging on insulin, with the district facing potential costs from a settlement. Superintendent Patricia Saelens noted that the fair price of insulin is around $35 per vial. The board reached a consensus to consider joining the action after a review and consultation with the school district attorney.

title: Learn beekeeping basics
content: The Cecil County Public Library is offering a free class called "The Basics of Beekeeping" on October 16 at 6:30-8:30 p.m. at Rising Sun branch (111 Colonial Way). Jane Bellmyer will teach the class. Registration is required, and can be done online at https://www.cecilcountylibrary.org/event/buzzing-knowledge-discover-basics-beekeeping-63433.

title: Chess for kids, teens at Talbot library
content: The Talbot County Free Library is hosting a chess event for kids and teens ages 8 to 16 on October 23 at the downtown Easton branch from 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Registration is required at https://talbot.librarycalendar.com/event/afternoon-chess-170

title: Focus remains clear
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 3 sentences:

Ann O'Connor, candidate for Talbot County Board of Education, clarifies that she has not received endorsements from Mom's For Liberty despite attending local M4L Chapter meetings. Her focus remains on prioritizing the needs of children, teachers, and parental involvement to improve the school system. O'Connor's platform is guided by principles of Advancing Academics, Boosting Accountability, and Cultivating Character if elected to the school board.

title: Candidates have varying views
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

In the 2024 election season, voters in Talbot County will choose representatives for the school board from six candidates with varying views on education. Conservative candidates Ann O'Connor, Karla Wieland-Cherry, and Kerry Gunshenan are running alongside progressive candidates Cynthia Jurrius, Anna Howie, and Candace Henry. A debate hosted by Moms for Liberty featured four of the six candidates, while a separate event at the Avalon Theater included only three progressive candidates. The Talbot County Democratic Forum sponsored another debate at the Academy Art Museum with only two conservative candidates invited to speak.

title: Karla Wieland-Cherry
content: Karla Wieland-Cherry, a 55-year-old resident of Trappe, is running for the District 5 seat on the Talbot County Board of Education. She aims to improve the local school system by attracting more qualified teachers, raising education standards, and increasing the use of CTE programs. Wieland-Cherry prioritizes rebuilding trust with teachers and addressing safety concerns in schools.

title: Anna Howie
content: Anna Howie, a resident of Easton and assistant principal at Federalsburg Elementary School, was appointed to the Talbot County Board of Education by Gov. Wes Moore in October 2023. She is running for re-election on issues such as increasing student achievement in math and reading, recruiting quality teachers, and addressing the district's fiscal responsibility. Howie supports the Blueprint For Maryland's Future, citing its focus on early childhood education, diverse teachers, and resources for students' success. Her priorities align with those of Dr. Shraron Pepukayi, the superintendent of Talbot County Public Schools.

title: Cynthia Marrah Jurrius
content: Cynthia Marrah Jurris, a 65-year-old Easton resident and mediation law expert, is running for the District 6 seat on the Talbot County Board of Education. She is married with three sons who graduated from Talbot County Public Schools. Her priorities include fostering academic excellence, supporting educators, and creating a thriving school environment. The most important issue facing Talbot County Public Schools is advancing academic proficiency, which can be addressed by providing innovative support, engaging families, and using technology effectively.

title: Ann O'Connor
content: Ann O'Connor, a 55-year-old Easton resident, is running for the District 2 seat on the Talbot County Board of Education as a former teacher and mother of six. She prioritizes advancing academics, boosting accountability, and cultivating character. The most important issue facing Talbot County Public Schools is the steady decline of academic rigor, which O'Connor aims to address through increased emphasis on traditional learning methods and early intervention in elementary schools.

title: Candace Henry
content: Candace Henry, a Talbot County Board of Education member, is running for reelection. She is the director of the Disability Resource Center at Salisbury University and lives in Easton with her family. Henry's priorities include narrowing opportunity gaps, improving special education services, and recruiting high-quality educators if reelected. The most pressing issue facing TCPS is addressing the reading and math proficiency gap, which she aims to solve by investing in targeted interventions and educator support.

title: Kerry Gunshenan
content: Kerry Gunshenan is a regional sales director for Evoke Pharma who lives in Easton and serves as chairman of the Talbot County Public Schools Advisory Council and president of the St. Michaels YMCA Advisory Board. She has been married for 22 years and has five children, aged 14-20. Gunshenan is running for the District 6 seat on the Board of Education, citing a decline in education quality since her oldest child started school. Her priorities include ensuring students are college or career ready by graduation and addressing issues such as declining standardized test scores.

title: Easton Middle to pilot cell phone pouches in December
content: Easton Middle School will pilot a cell phone pouch system in December, following the lead of other school districts. The program aims to restrict student cell phone use during class instruction. Talbot County Public Schools has partnered with Yondr to provide 975 cell phone pouches for $26,900, which will be paid from the local budget. The pilot is expected to run throughout the year and may extend to other schools in the district if deemed successful.

title: Talbot Board of Ed approves funding for capital projects, discusses turf field status
content: The Talbot Board of Education approved funding for capital projects, including Easton High auditorium lights ($817,321) and LED lights at St. Michaels Middle/High School ($566,000), with $117,000 allocated to athletic field projects in general. The board discussed the potential for an artificial turf field at Easton High, but no official motion was made due to concerns over safety and prioritization. Talbot County Public Schools has $1.5 million in fiscal year 2025 funding from the county to allocate towards capital projects.

title: Safe havens of knowledge
content: Thomas Jefferson believed that an informed citizenry was essential to a democracy's success. The American Library Association released preliminary data documenting 414 attempts to censor library materials and services in public, school, and academic libraries during the first eight months of 2024, with 47% targeting books representing people of color and LGBTQ+ voices. Banned Books Week is being commemorated on October 19, Freedom to Read Day of Action, by Unite Against Book Bans.

title: Thoughts on smart phone restrictions in schools
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

Pew Research Center reports that 95% of teenagers have access to smartphones, and many schools are implementing restrictions on phone use during school days. Social psychologist Jonathan Stephen Haidt suggests that these restrictions may not address deeper-seated issues, such as a decline in play-based childhood and the rise of phone-based childhood. Haidt argues that this combination has robbed generations of opportunities to develop resilience and independence, leading to unprecedented levels of anxiety among American youth. He recommends delaying smartphone use until high school and giving children basic phones instead of smartphones. Parents and guardians must make unpopular but necessary decisions to set limits on their young people's phone use for their own good.

title: Dorchester ends alternative education contract in middle, elementary schools
content: Dorchester County Board of Education unanimously voted to terminate its one-year contract with Transforming Lives for convenience, ending alternative education services for up to 48 elementary and middle school students starting from a future date, as specified by the contract. The contract's terms require either party to provide 60-day advance written notice for termination. This decision comes after the board previously terminated its three-year contract with Vision Quest in June 2024.

title: Group promotes extremist agenda
content: Moms for Liberty is an extremist group advancing an anti-student inclusion agenda that was included as an extremist group by the Southern Poverty Law Center. The group has a chapter in Talbot County and three members on the Department of Education workgroup overseeing school libraries. Influential leaders include Ann O'Connor, Karla Wieland-Cherry, Kerry Gunshenan, and Candace Henry.

title: 6 candidates vie for 3 seats on Talbot Board of Education
content: Six candidates are running for three seats on the Talbot County Board of Education in the November 5 general election. The positions up for election are Districts 2, 5, and 6, with each serving a four-year term from December 1, 2024 to December 1, 2028. Early voting begins October 24 through October 31 at the Easton Fire House Bingo Hall, while polling places can be found on talbotcountymd.org.

title: Should Maryland schools ban cellphones?
content: Maryland's school board candidates largely support stricter cellphone policies in schools, with 64 of 74 candidates favoring restrictions. The policies vary by county, but some aim to minimize cellphone use during instructional time. Annette Anderson, deputy director of the Johns Hopkins Center for Safe and Healthy Schools, cites concerns over mental health, internet addiction, and social connectivity. Many candidates cite disciplinary issues, cyberbullying, and phone addiction as reasons for restricting cellphone use.

title: Maryland school board candidates push for officers, mental health services
content:
Here is a summary of the article:

Maryland school board candidates advocate for adding more law enforcement officers and mental health services to address school safety concerns. Candidates in various districts call for increased school resource officers, while others emphasize the need for counselors, social-emotional learning, and stricter discipline measures. Violent incidents in schools have increased nationwide, with Maryland seeing a 49% rise in violent incidents in the 2023-2024 school year.

title: Is Maryland’s ‘Blueprint’ the path to better schools?
content: Maryland's 'Blueprint for Maryland's Future,' a $30 billion plan to improve public schools, is being debated among school board candidates, with some expressing concerns about its costs and mandates. The Blueprint was passed in 2021 by the General Assembly and aims to boost teacher salaries, expand pre-kindergarten, adjust the curriculum, implement a "ninth-grade tracker" system, and boost funding. Governor Wes Moore has acknowledged that the plan may need adjustments due to long-term deficits projected by the state Department of Legislative Services.

title: Author empowering young voices
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Jessieca Montgomery, an educator and author, has created a series of coloring and activity books on public speaking for kids in grades kindergarten through 5. The series aims to help young learners build confidence and express themselves effectively by combining creativity with essential communication skills. Key titles include "Speak and Shine," "Confidence in Every Word," and "The Little Speaker's Toolkit." Montgomery's approach emphasizes inclusivity, representation, and storytelling, empowering children from diverse backgrounds to see themselves in the material.

title: Parties should stay out of school elections
content: The Maryland Democratic Party will spend tens of thousands of dollars targeting school board candidates it claims support a "hateful" and "right-wing agenda." The party plans to hire canvassers and provide resources to local Democratic central committees for supporting candidates with "Democratic and inclusive values." In response, some argue that state and local political parties should not be involved in non-partisan school elections.

title: Experience, transparency needed
content: The article discusses the upcoming Talbot County school board election between Candace Henry and Ann O'Connor. The author initially considered both candidates but found that Candace Henry is more knowledgeable about the state of schools and has experience. However, flyers promoting Ann O'Connor have raised concerns due to cherry-picked data and questionable funding sources, including the 1776 Project.

title: Collaborative, open-minded partner
content: Cynthia Jurrius is an independent candidate running for District 6 representative on the Talbot County school board. She stands out as a strong advocate for fostering inclusive and safe educational environments. Cynthia's experience, values, and vision align with community needs, and her professional background as a mediator will be invaluable to the board.

title: Tench Tilghman: A Talbot County-born revolutionary hero
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Tench Tilghman was born in Talbot County in 1744 and became one of George Washington's most trusted men during the Revolutionary War.
Tilghman joined Washington's staff in 1776 and played a critical role in the Battle of Yorktown, delivering the notice of British surrender.
He died in 1786, but his legacy continues to be celebrated with the Tench Tilghman Week, sponsored by the Colonel Tench Tilghman Chapter of the Maryland Society of the Sons of the American Revolution.

title: An open letter on recent education mailers
content: Talbot County Public Schools' Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi and Board President Emily Jackson wrote an open letter addressing recent education mailers that unfairly targeted their schools and educators. They highlighted investments in new curricula and teacher retention, with modest improvement in state assessments in the 2023-24 school year. The district shows growth, including a significant increase in English/Language Arts proficiency among students. Pepukayi and Jackson invited the community to public forums and encouraged collaboration for student success.

title: Ridgely Elementary School students get into the Halloween spirit
content: Students, teachers and staff participated in Ridgely Elementary School's annual Halloween parade on October 31, 2024, lined with Central Avenue. The event was organized by Clerk-Treasurer Stephanie Berkey, who started the idea in the early 2000s. Since 2011, Berkey and Assistant Clerk-Treasurer Melissa Leonard have collaborated with 18 businesses that participated in handing out candy to students.

title: Students learn to build and sell in CBMM's Rising Tide After-School program
content: The Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum's Rising Tide After-School program provides middle school students with vocational skills education under volunteer supervision. The program, launched in 2017 as a boat building initiative, now focuses on marketing and entrepreneurship. Students create ornaments to sell in the museum's store, learning project design, team collaboration, and marketing skills. The program runs quarterly, offering partial to full scholarships and transportation for participants from St. Michaels and surrounding areas.

title: School mailing accusations are false
content: Talbot County residents received US Postal Service mailings criticizing the quality of teaching in local public schools, falsely attributing low English and math proficiency to "harmful gender ideology". The mailings originated from "Pay Attention America Inc." with a Delaware address. Talbot County Public Schools have high attendance and graduation rates, and are one of only eight Maryland districts with star ratings of three or higher.

title: Decline in social capital has reached new lows
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

Robert Putnam's 1995 book "Bowling Alone" analyzed the decline in social capital in American society starting from 1950. The author suggests this decline has worsened due to limited social interactions during the Covid-19 pandemic, particularly among young children. A recent incident at a GOP dinner in Talbot County highlights the need for renewed civic engagement and collaboration. Putnam's book and upcoming programs, such as the Chesapeake Forum and Baylor University webinar, offer opportunities for citizens to learn about and improve social capital.

title: Relationships key to positive change
content: Candace Henry is endorsed by Emily Moody for Talbot County School Board District 2 in a candidate forum. Candace Henry and her opponent share similar qualities as compassionate parents and community members. However, Candace Henry has demonstrated stronger relationships with students, teachers, parents, and staff, citing her knowledge of the Maryland Blueprint for Education and experience implementing it.

title: Your vote matters
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Candace Henry is a Talbot County school board candidate for District 2 who prioritizes creating a diverse and equitable atmosphere for all students. She brings decades of experience in education to the board and supports access to information and high-quality educational materials. The opposition, backed by Moms for Liberty, seeks to restrict LGBTQ+ protections and divide the student body. Henry is running on a platform of excellence, equity, and inclusivity, and voters are urged to support her in District 2.

title: Talbot County schools remain beacon of opportunity, excellence
content: Talbot County Public Schools are facing criticism over recent mailers targeting them, but the district claims to be addressing challenges with transparency. The 23-24 Maryland Comprehensive Assessment results showed modest improvement across all districts, including Talbot County's slight margin of progress and greatest increase in English language arts proficiency. The district adheres to health education standards set by the Maryland Department of Education and prioritizes math education. Talbot County students graduate to excel in college and careers, and the community is invited to public forums with the school system.

title: Talbot Board of Education may see new faces in December
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Unofficial results published by the Maryland Board of Elections show Ann O'Connor leading Candace Henry in District 2 with 54.5% of the vote. Karla Wieland-Cherry won District 5 with 56.4% of the votes counted, while Cynthia Jurrius led Kerry Gunshenan in District 6 with 50.4% of the vote. The winners will serve five-year terms on the Talbot County Board of Education starting December 1.

title: Wheedleton wins Dorchester Board of Education seat
content: Chris Wheedleton won the District 5 Board of Education seat in Dorchester County with 69.5% of the vote as of November 5, 2024. He was appointed to the board in 2023 and plans to maintain his focus on putting students first, empowering teachers, and involving the community. Unopposed candidates Brandy Dawson Cumberland (District 1) and Christine LaMonica (District 3) received 97.8% and 97.9% of votes, respectively, also appointed by the Dorchester County Council in July 2024.

title: Student vets' stories provide unique insight on service
content:
Veterans at Elizabeth City's institutions of higher education shared their experiences and how serving in the military affected their lives and career choices. 
Bobby Martin, a U.S. Navy veteran, served from 1977 to joined his father, a Vietnam-era veteran and minister, as a role model. Wendra Costly, a U.S. Army veteran, left the military in 2018 seeking a long-term career with good pay. Michelle Barnes, also an ECSU student, spent eight years in the Navy, enlisting at age 25.
Veterans from College of The Albemarle (COA), Mid-Atlantic Christian University (MACU), and Elizabeth City State University (ECSU) attended a Veterans Day observance on November 8, 2024, sharing their stories.

title: Athens High School holds Veterans Day event for students
content: Athens High School held a Veterans Day event for students to talk and hear from veterans in Athens County. The assembly featured Chad Springer, an associate superintendent at Athens City Schools and former United States Army sergeant, who shared his experience with students. Springer recounted his uncles' military service during World War II and the Korean War. According to US Census Bureau data, 6.2% of adults are veterans, but this number has fallen significantly since 2005.

title: Midshore Technology Services to work with student apprentice
content: Kyren Hawkins signed a youth apprenticeship contract with Justin Smith, president of Midshore Technology Services in Denton, on November 12, 2024. Hawkins is currently enrolled in cybersecurity at North Caroline High School. This is Midshore Technology Services' second youth apprenticeship agreement, with the first occurring in 2021 with Christopher Ireland.

title: Haven Ministries welcomes opening of Jacob Sloan Center
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The Jacob Sloan Center, an extension of Haven Ministries emergency shelter, opened with a ribbon-cutting at the Shore Christian Fellowship Church on October 31, 2024.
Haven Ministries executive director Peter Grim described the center as providing life skills education, including resume writing and finances, to individuals in need.
Jake Sloan's parents, Mary and Peter Sloan, partnered with Haven Ministries to continue their son's legacy after his death in a car accident in 2018 at age 12.
The Jacob Sloan Foundation has provided funding for the center, with additional support from Tim and Linette Miller.

title: It's been a wild ride
content: Robbi Behr and Matthew Swanson, authors of children's novels, embarked on a "Busload of Books Tour" to visit Title I schools in every state over a year. Their literacy initiative aims to provide better access to books for kids in underfunded schools. The couple, supported by educational researchers from Washington College, visited 12 schools across the US, including six in-person and six virtually. They were invited to speak at the Masters of Scale Conference in San Francisco, where they adapted their presentation to appeal to an adult audience.

title: Maryland conservatives make gains in school board races
content: Conservative school board candidates won control in Somerset and Calvert counties, while appearing poised to win in Talbot County. The 1776 Project PAC's endorsed candidates won or narrowly led their races in 11 districts statewide. Maryland Democrats targeted 24 "extreme" conservative candidates, with only nine losing so far.

title: St. Michaels temporary library opens at Village Shopping Center
content: The Talbot County Free Library's St. Michaels Branch has opened a temporary location at the Village Shopping Center on November 13, 2024. The library is serving residents of St. Michaels until its main branch on Fremont Street undergoes a 12-18 month construction expansion. The temporary location offers most full-service library amenities, including children's materials and audio books, but lacks meeting rooms and an external book drop. Shauna Beulah, branch manager, and Diana Hastings, youth services librarian, are available for comment.

title: Mother can't provide holiday celebration while in school
content: A mother of three is in school to obtain her nursing certification and struggles to provide a holiday celebration for her children due to living expenses and school costs. The Brighter Christmas Fund, a nonprofit helping families in need on the Mid-Shore, will assist with her family's holiday celebration. Donations can be sent to The Star Democrat at 29088 Airpark Dr., Easton, MD 21601 or made online via credit card or PayPal. As of November 15, 2024, the total donated for this year's Brighter Christmas Fund is $27,643.75.

title: Local seniors inducted into hall of fame
content: Phil Cicconi and Ted Clark were inducted into the Maryland Senior Citizens Hall of Fame for 2024. They were honored at a luncheon on October 17, 2023, at Ten Oaks Ballroom in Clarksville, Maryland, alongside other 24 inductees. Cicconi is a dedicated community leader who has made significant contributions to Kent County through various initiatives, including the Kent County Learning Center and conservation efforts. Clark was recognized for his volunteer services in the community. The Maryland Senior Citizens Hall of Fame was established in 1987 to publicly recognize senior citizens ages 65+ who have performed outstanding service in their communities.

title: Newcomers win Talbot County Board of Education seats
content: Cynthia Marrah Jurrius, Karla Wieland-Cherry, and Ann O'Connor won seats on the Talbot County Board of Education in November 2024 elections. The newcomers will begin their four-year terms on December 1. O'Connor prioritizes academics and discipline, while Wieland-Cherry focuses on open communication and promoting the Career and Technology Education Program. Jurrius won District 6 with 51.9% of the vote.

title: Student-parents need support from colleges
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Mike Muñoz, president of Long Beach City College, emphasizes the need for colleges to support student-parents who face numerous obstacles, including housing and food insecurity, and lack of affordable child care. According to college data, most student-parents are mothers of color who identify as single and are facing financial disadvantages. The college offers various resources, including a Child Development Center and cost-free after-school care, to support student-parents, with plans to expand these services through partnerships like Raise The Barr and Ascend at the Aspen Institute's Postsecondary Leadership Circle Activation Fund.

title: Maryland schools get new rules for shooter drills
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Maryland schools will implement new guidelines for active shooter drills starting in 2025, prohibiting trauma-inducing elements and requiring parental notification. The guidelines aim to limit the impact on students' mental health and increase communication between staff, parents, and students. The Maryland Center for School Safety released the guidelines as part of a state law requiring them to draft new parameters after concerns about the drills' psychological impact were raised nationwide. Del. Jared Solomon sponsored the measure, citing anxiety among young people due to school shootings.

title: Talbot County Education Foundation honors 3 alumni
content: Keasha Haythe, JoAnn Asparagus Murray, and Ludwig Eglseder III were honored by Talbot County Public Schools as the district's 2024 Distinguished Alumni on November 15, 2024, at the Oxford Community Center. The event raised funds for projects and initiatives in the school district, including a student leadership program and pre-kindergarten language and literacy. Haythe graduated from Easton High School in 1991, while Asparagus Murray attended Robert Russa Moton High School before moving to Philadelphia, graduating in the 11th grade. Eglseder graduated from St. Michaels High School in 1975.

title: Character Counts celebrates 24th anniversary
content: Character Counts celebrated its 24th anniversary on November 12, 2024, with recognition from Queen Anne's County Commissioners. The initiative was launched in fall 2000, following the Columbine tragedy, and has since reached approximately 70,000 to 100,000 students. Character Counts Coaches are now present in 10 county pre-k classrooms and all Queen Anne's County middle and elementary schools, with over 4,200 students receiving character education experiences this year.

title: Talbot Board of Ed bids farewell to 3 outgoing board members
content: Talbot County Board of Education bid farewell to outgoing members Candace Henry, Anna Howie, and Mary Wheeler at a monthly meeting on November 22, 2024. Three new members will be sworn in next month. The departing board members served for 7.5 years (Wheeler), 1.5 years (Howie), and an unspecified time (Henry). They were thanked by Superintendent Sharon Pepukayi for their service to the schools.

title: Ravens flock; Local kids honored at NFL game
content: The Kent Island High School Interact Club was honored by the Baltimore Ravens with the National Football League team's Honor Rows distinction on October 13. The award recognized their commitment to community service and leadership development, led by teacher Lacey Phelps and in partnership with the Giving the Edge Foundation. The Leadership Cohort program started in 2021 at Kent Island High School and has grown to over 40+ students who volunteer before school to discuss their passions. On November 22, 2024, nearly 50 students attended a Ravens game against the Washington Commanders and were celebrated for their contributions.

title: DCPS not moving forward with new alternative education programming
content: Dorchester County Public Schools terminated contracts with alternative education companies in October and November 2023 for elementary and middle school students and high schoolers, respectively. DCPS Superintendent Jymil Thompson recommended not pursuing new contracts due to budgetary restraints. The district will continue staffing its Positive Change Academy on Glasgow Street.

title: DCPS to examine oldest elementary school buildings as teachers demand change
content: Sandy Hill Elementary School teachers in Cambridge, MD demanded change due to old and deteriorating buildings. The Dorchester County Board of Education voted to have architecture firm Hord Coplan Macht do an ed specifications and feasibility study for the district's oldest elementary schools, including Sandy Hill. The study is funded by Maryland's Interagency Commission on School Construction, which estimates $2.75 million in funding for Dorchester County for fiscal year 2026. Assistant Superintendent Michael Collins said the process will take six months to complete, with a committee working with the community to determine ideal school designs and feasibility.

title: 'Share and make merry': International students get a taste of American holidays
content: International students from around the world attended a Thanksgiving dinner sponsored by the University of Delaware's Center for Global Programs & Services on November 24, 2024. Approximately 500 international students and family members joined 500 local university staff and faculty for a traditional American turkey dinner. The event, now in its 11th year, aims to introduce international students to an American tradition and build community among the student body.

title: Caroline Commissioners hear update on potential for new middle school
content: Caroline County Commissioners heard an update on potential plans for a new middle school in November 2024. Bill Mengel, director of operations at Caroline County Public Schools, presented a revised fiscal year 2026 capital improvement plan that includes funding for a potential new middle school building. The county will be responsible for around 11% of the total $86 million estimation for years one and two, with a main point of negotiation being "How do we get more square footage?" Mengel noted that cost per square foot has risen sharply year to year, potentially reaching $490 per square foot by FY30.

title: St. Michaels residents donate hygiene supplies for student success
content: Four St. Michaels residents donate hygiene supplies, including dental floss, toothbrushes, and feminine hygiene products, in collaboration with St. Michaels Middle/High School to support student success. The initiative began in September 2024 after a back-to-school event was told the church had all necessary supplies, led by Kevin and Marybeth Sullivan and supported by Commissioner Jay Hudson and Katrina Whittington.

title: Four Eleven Kitchen aims to feed minds and bellies through food access program
content: Four Eleven Kitchen's Feed The People program aims to provide food access through a recurring community supper event and an urban "learning" farm in Cambridge, MD. Founded by Amanda Kidd in 2016, the nonprofit has partnered with the City of Cambridge and Habitat for Humanity to turn two parcels into an educational resource center. The goal is to reduce barriers to resources and opportunities, targeting a "starvation of knowledge and education." Feed The People's programs aim to feed both bodies and minds through cooking skills, farm-to-table education, and nutrition.

title: Gala at Kennard honors former educators
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 sentences:

Queen Anne's County Commissioners pledged $50,000 annually for three years to support Kennard African American Cultural Heritage Center and Museum (KAACHC), with a total funding commitment of $140,000, including an initial $50,000 check presented on Nov. 9. The center will hire an executive director by January 1, 2025, to manage programs and operations. Former Kennard High School educators Dr. Velma Kennedy Speight, Madelyn Matthews Hollis, and Alveta Smith Jones were honored for their dedication to education. The center has become a vital resource for African American heritage in Queen Anne's County, offering various programs and exhibits since its restoration completed in 2019.

title: New Beginnings Youth and Family Services honors Theresa Stafford with name change
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

New Beginnings Youth and Family Services will be renamed Dr. Theresa Stafford's New Beginnings Learning Academy in honor of its late executive director. The name change was made possible by donations from individuals who wanted to preserve the legacy of Theresa Stafford, who served as executive director until her death in December 2023.
