Phil Feldman donated $25,000 to help secure the name change. A ribbon cutting and dedication ceremony will be held on November 30 at noon to unveil the center's new sign. The event coincides with what would have been Stafford's 71st birthday and aims to celebrate her legacy and continue creating opportunities for children.

title: Governor puts $1.8 million toward making Maryland a 'cyber capital'
content: Gov. Wes Moore announced a $1.8 million award to Maryland's 16 community colleges to boost cybersecurity training and career opportunities. The funding comes from the Accelerating Cyber Careers grant by the Maryland Department of Labor and will be provided by BCR Cyber, a private company that offers cybersecurity training programs and job placement services.

title: More than half of Talbot County students receive free and reduced lunches
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Talbot County Public Schools reported that over half of its students receive free and reduced lunches, with rates as high as 76% at Easton Elementary School. Food insecurity is on the rise in Talbot County, where costs of food, housing, and other necessities outpace salary growth. The Maryland Department of Education found a 13% increase in free and reduced meals from the previous school year to 2022-2023. Gov. Wes Moore signed a state Senate bill requiring reporting of costs to provide universal free school meals to all public school students in Maryland.

title: MSDE announces 2024 Maryland School Report Card
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 5 concise sentences:

The Maryland State Department of Education released the 2024 Maryland School Report Card data on December 3. School ratings have increased overall compared to the 2022-23 academic year. 41% of schools earned a four- or five-star rating, while 83% earned three stars or more. Deputy State Superintendent Geoff Sanderson reported that nearly twice as many schools increased their star rating than decreased it. The MSDE is working to improve its accountability system to be more sensitive to granularity growth and develop different benchmark systems for data collection.

title: Caroline Board of Ed welcomes new members, elects president
content: Chrissy Bartz and Stefanie Johnson were sworn in as new members of the Caroline County Board of Education, along with Michele Wayman who was unanimously elected as president. Michele Wayman previously worked at Caroline County Public Schools for 36 years before retiring in 2009. Chrissy Bartz is director of community-based programs at Choptank Community Health and ran unopposed in District 1. Stefanie Johnson, who also ran unopposed, is executive director of His Hope Ministries shelter and board member for the Caroline County Chamber of Commerce.

title: Maintaining parental rights
content: Lena Gill's letter was responded to by Mary-Eileen Russell, who wrote on December 7, 2024. Russell clarified that Ann O'Connor and Karla Wieland-Cherry are not members of Moms for Liberty. Russell described Moms for Liberty as a support group advocating for maintaining parental rights through grades K-12, providing resources and information on educational trends. The group's agenda includes changes in curriculum and policies, such as better scores and reduced violence, opposed by many parents, including Superintendent Dr. Sharon Pepukayi.

title: Ella Morton, 100, celebrated by her former 3rd grade Trappe Elementary class
content: Ella Morton, 100, celebrated by her former 3rd grade Trappe Elementary class at Easton Elks Lodge on December 7, 2024. She taught at Trappe Elementary School for over 20 years, turning 100 on May 24, 2024. Many of her former students remembered Morton as their "favorite teacher" and recalled how she was kind, genuinely nice, and controlled the classroom.

title: DCPS 'encouraged' by 2024 Maryland School Report Card
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The 2024 Maryland School Report Card results showed improvement in Dorchester County Public Schools, with North Dorchester Middle School and Mace's Lane Middle School gaining stars for academic achievement. The district saw increases in English language arts and math proficiency, graduation rates, and attendance, but still faces a goal to move from 23rd to 15th in academic performance statewide within four years. Superintendent Jymil Thompson emphasized the need for continued focus on targeted strategies and interventions to achieve this goal.

title: Caroline superintendent projects 'good budget year,' discusses Blueprint
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Derek Simmons, Caroline County Superintendent, projects a "good budget year" for fiscal year 2026. The district's revenue numbers are contingent on state legislative actions, with Simmons expecting a clear picture by mid-April at best. Simmons emphasizes the importance of salaries and maintaining adequate staffing levels, particularly in light of the state's Blueprint initiative requiring minimum teacher salaries to reach $26,000 by July 2026.

title: BAAM plans ceremony for new academic center
content: Building African American Minds (BAAM) Inc. announced a ribbon-cutting ceremony for its new academic center on December 14, 2024, at 10 a.m. The event will be held at BAAM Athletic Center in Easton, MD, featuring remarks from organizational leaders and community partners. Dina Gomes Daly, executive director of BAAM, described the center as a "space where learning, growth and community come alive."

title: Easton Middle School drops a star in Maryland School Report Card
content: Easton Middle School lost a star in the 2024 Maryland School Report Card, dropping from three stars and 48th percentile to two stars and 32nd percentile. The school scored 44 points, down from 46.1 in 2023. Debbie Gardner, Talbot County Public Schools' Director of Communications, stated that the district is "closely examining" the report card results and sees opportunities for data collection and analysis.

title: Noam Chomsky at 96: The linguist, educator, philosopher and public thinker has had a massive intellectual and moral influence
content:
Noam Chomsky, linguist, educator, philosopher and public thinker, turned 96 years old on Dec. 7, 2024. He was born Avram Noam Chomsky on Dec. 7, 1928, in Philadelphia. 

Chomsky's work focused on human creativity, attacking those who seek to control people, and promoting individual freedom and dignity. His interest in innate human abilities drew from philosophical treatises in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Chomsky challenged a structuralist paradigm in linguistics, proposing that humans are endowed with universal grammar and can learn language through innate knowledge. His work gained recognition in linguistics, philosophy, and psychology by the early 1960s. He was critical of big data, artificial intelligence, and ChatGPT, advocating for human rights, intellectual self-defense, and independent thinking.

Chomsky's legacy includes a significant influence on cognitive sciences and his continued publication and public speaking until his mid-90s.

title: MACo's Blueprint panelists stress importance of local context at session in Cambridge
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

Garrett County Blueprint Coordinator Nicole Miller emphasized the importance of local context during a session at the Maryland Association of Counties Winter Conference in Cambridge. Panelists, including Christina Miller and Derek Simmons, recommended revisiting the Blueprint due to funding challenges and inequities in implementation. St. Mary's County Commissioner Mike Hewitt expressed concern about raising county taxes for the Blueprint, while Sen. Mary Beth Carozza stated that Gov. Wes Moore is willing to make adjustments to the plan.

title: Dorchester BOE votes to keep staffing Positive Change Academy through school year
content: Dorchester County Public Schools will continue to provide alternative education through its Positive Change Academy with staffing provided by PASS Educators, a substitute and permanent staffing provider from Delaware. The program serves pre-K through second graders in the district. A new agreement allows the current staff to finish out the school year after Transforming Lives' contract was set to expire imminently.

title: Dorchester BOE reelects leadership, new members sworn in
content:
Here is a concise summary of the article:

The Dorchester County Board of Education reelected President Sheri Hubbard and Vice President Talibah Chikwendu for another year. New members Brandy Dawson Cumberland, Christine LaMonica, and Chris Wheedleton were sworn in for their first full term, replacing former board members Mike Diaz, Susan Morgan, and Laura Layton.

title: 'Vision from the beginning': BAAM leaders excited for new academic center
content: Building African American Minds Inc.'s new academic center in Easton, Maryland is expected to open in January 2025. The $10 million project, funded by private donors, community donations, and state and federal funding, will house classes, tutoring, youth programs, and more. Dina Daly, executive director of Building African American Minds, has been leading the organization since its founding as a boys-only nonprofit in 2005. The new center is expected to significantly expand the nonprofit's reach and services, including adult workforce programs hosted by Chesapeake College.

title: University of Delaware to pay $700K to settle claims it failed to disclose professor's ties to China
content: The University of Delaware agreed to pay $700,000 to settle claims it failed to disclose professor Xiao-Hai Yan's ties to China when accepting a NASA grant in 2020. UD accepted the grant despite knowing Yan had ties to China and participated in a program to recruit individuals with foreign technology intellectual property knowledge. Xiao-Hai Yan is a faculty member at Xiamen University in China. The settlement does not constitute an admission of liability by UD, but rather a strategic decision to avoid litigation.

title: UD to pay $700K to settle claims it failed to disclose professor's ties to China
content:
Here is a summary of the article in 2-5 concise sentences:

The University of Delaware agreed to pay over $700,000 to settle claims it failed to disclose professor Xiao-Hai Yan's ties to China when accepting a NASA grant in 2020. Yan has been a UD professor since 1990 and participates in a Chinese government program to recruit individuals with foreign technology intellectual property knowledge.
